Kanau Manual

A lighting console for film and television, built for iPhone. Control fixtures over Art-Net, sACN and CRMX, with color, Scenes, effects and diagnostics in your pocket.

What's new

The main changes in each version, newest first. Each chapter has the details.

1.1 (378)

  • Two fixtures on overlapping addresses can both be used. An overlapping address sends the value of the fixture you moved last. On Home, a red ! sits above the value (chapter 03).
  • A patched Kanau Lite is easier to work. It is named Lite 1, Back 1 and Vibe 1 when patched. Rows such as Cells and Content read as the name you chose, and Playback has play, pause and restart buttons (chapter 03).
  • In the ULTIMATE modes, the faders of cells that are not on the Kanau Lite screen are dimmed (chapter 03).

1.1 (377)

  • MOVE has a row of section buttons at the top. Of POSITION, GOBO, BEAM, FOCUS and SHAPERS, only the one you tap is shown. The Focus row stays in the same place whichever section is open (chapter 07).
  • The Focus row in MOVE has FINE. Focus and continuous values such as zoom move by 1/10 of your finger (chapter 07).
  • A continuous value such as zoom or frost is one row, even across different models (chapter 07).
  • BATTERY SAVE now sets the brightness the fixtures keep: 75%, 50%, 35%, 25% or 0%. At 0% only the BATTERY SAVE fixtures go out (chapter 10).
  • When addresses overlap, both fixtures are marked. This is the same in the Patch List, its PDF and the Re-patch list (chapter 03).

1.0 (374)

  • Kanau Pro now comes as MONTHLY or LIFETIME, a single payment. The yearly plan is gone. The first month of MONTHLY is still free (chapter 03).

1.0 (372)

  • Settings has a Kanau Free line at the top. It turns into Kanau Pro in amber while you have Kanau Pro. Tap it to open the Kanau Pro purchase screen (chapter 03).
  • LITE MODE can show images and videos. Add them to Media from the Photos app or from files, and the Media channel of FX & MEDIA and ULTIMATE picks them (chapter 02).
  • Kanau Screen is now Kanau Lite. Mode names start with a mode number. The Function channel is gone, so every mode except BACK LIGHT ONLY has one channel fewer. Whether the screen goes dark at your ear is set with PROXIMITY in LITE MODE (chapters 02 and 03). Fixtures patched as Kanau Screen in 1.0 (371) or earlier no longer match the channel order, so patch them again as Kanau Lite.
  • Fixture Usage can be narrowed to one model or group (chapter 11).

1.0 (371)

  • LITE MODE has 19 modes. COOKIE splits the screen into dappled areas, and ULTIMATE chooses how to split the screen and can show patterns too. Kanau Screen in Patch has the same 19 modes (chapters 02 and 03).
  • STRIPS now run along the long side of the screen. On an upright screen they are numbered from the top (chapter 02).

1.0 (370)

  • LITE MODE has 15 modes. STRIPS split the screen into vertical strips, and FX & MEDIA puts moving patterns on it. Kanau Screen in Patch has the same 15 modes (chapters 02 and 03).
  • While on Free, what is not sent is marked: a red 1–64 on the row with ‹／›, a red double line on the Patch screen, and a red × in DMX Monitor (chapter 03).
  • In Groups, ‹／› moves only within the group (chapter 04).

0.2 (368)

  • Fixture Usage is new. It keeps a record of which fixtures were touched and when, on this device for 180 days. It opens from Settings → Settings (chapter 11).
  • While you reorder Home, the button on the ⏻ row makes that fixture draw one peak of brightness (chapter 04).
  • The Patch form has TOGETHER and FILL GAPS. FILL GAPS puts fixtures one by one into free space (chapter 03).
  • The ZEN TILT angles can also be set in Settings → Settings (chapter 04).
  • In MIDI, Faders & Switches folds too, and Last Note shows notes. The order of Buttons has changed (chapter 12).
  • Switching TOGETHER and SPREAD or the arrangement of a running effect now crosses over in the effect's fade-in time. ORBIT, BOX, SPIRAL and BREATHE turn around the position you placed, and LIGHTHOUSE swings Tilt on a fixture with no Pan (chapter 09).
  • For most models whose data has no angles, Pan and Tilt now read in degrees (chapter 07).

0.2 (367)

  • LAMP MODE is now LITE MODE. The button that starts it is LITE MODE START (chapter 02). BACK LIGHT ONLY is no longer listed on a device with no back light.
  • The Patch form now shows the free space from the address you typed, and Map has a Universe pulldown (chapter 03).
  • In Re-patch, Universe and Address can now be typed (chapter 06).
  • On PIXELS, GRADIENT's START and END now hold an intensity as well as a color. Modes with only Hue and Saturation can use the PIXELS layouts too (chapter 05).
  • DMX Monitor has a Universe pulldown (chapter 02).

0.2 (366)

  • ZEN's TILT now stays at the bottom when you lower the top edge below flat, and the value does not jump in any position (chapter 04).

0.2 (365)

  • ZEN's TILT now keeps vibrating while it stays at the top, and vibrates once on reaching the bottom (chapter 04).

0.2 (364)

  • Kanau Screen has nine modes. BACK LIGHT ONLY uses just the back light, and the rest are one screen or 2, 4 or 8 parts, each in RGB or HUE SAT. CCT, G/M, Crossfade and Function channels are new, and the order has changed. A device on an earlier mode becomes SCREEN RGB 10ch, keeping its Universe and Address. On the other console, patch it again in the same mode as MODE on the device (chapters 02 and 03).
  • ZEN's TILT can now choose the angle for 0 as well. 0 AT is 0°, 15°, 30° or 45° and 100 AT is 90°, 60° or 45° (chapter 04).
  • In command entry, THRU can go on as many times as you like. 1 THRU 5 AT 0 THRU 100 THRU 0 gives 0, 50, 100, 50, 0 (chapter 08).
  • In and Out are gone from Advanced in effects. The time to come in and go out stays at each kind's starting value (chapter 09).

0.2 (363)

  • On iPhone, SETUP at the top of the panel now lights while you are looking at the Settings below (chapter 05).

0.2 (362)

  • A pixel's fader is now a percentage of its parent. The light that comes out is parent × cell ÷ 100. Lowering the parent leaves the cells' numbers and knobs where they are and marks the difference with an amber ↓. Raising a cell while the parent is at 0 does not raise the parent (chapter 04).
  • Test mode has more steps. FULL adds dimmer, built-in effects (MACRO) and a step for each kind of strobe, and BLINK can be chosen in Items. Color temperature also stops at 3200 K and 5600 K. The screen lists the values being sent, and ‹ / › step through a step one item at a time. Fixtures with lamps get STRIKE LAMP (chapter 06).
  • The Describe field, for making an effect from words, is no longer on the screen.

0.2 (361)

  • Test mode is now always available. Use Test Mode in Settings and Slide to test at the top of the panel are gone. Choose fixtures under TEST MODE at the bottom of SETUP in a fixture's panel, or under TEST MODE in Settings, and start with START TEST (chapter 06).
  • During the test, everything below the status line becomes the test screen: the current step, what is happening now (RED, PIXEL 5 / 16 and so on) and all the steps in order. Models with pixels get a PIXELS step (chapter 06).

0.2 (360)

  • Test mode is new. Turn on Use Test Mode under TEST MODE in Settings, and Slide to test in a fixture's panel runs a check of color temperature, color, gobos, head movement and more, built for each model. EXIT brings back the light from before the test (chapter 06).
  • Command entry: the @ key is now AT. GROUP 1 THRU 3, . 3 (pixels of the fixtures selected now) and 1 + 2 + 3 AT EFFECT can be typed. The SELECTED line under what you type shows the current selection. After an ENTER that sends a value, the selection is cleared (chapter 08).
  • If the light changes while nothing is being sent, the status at the top left turns red and reads Not sent. The first time you touch a fader while nothing is sent, Not sent shows above the faders (chapter 02).
  • A Scene's fade buttons are now fixed at SNAP, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2 and 3. Type any other time in the boxed field in the Scene's Settings (chapter 08).

0.2 (359)

  • Command entry now opens from COMMAND in the Play list. On iPad it is in the Play list in the rail on the left too. CMD in the Play row is gone (chapter 08).
  • Command entry has a FIXTURE key. FIXTURE 5 is the same as 5, and mixes with groups, as in GROUP 2 + FIXTURE 5 (chapter 08).

0.2 (358)

  • Command entry is new (iPhone). Open it with CMD in the Play row and type fixture numbers to select them: 1 THRU 50 − 25, @ 50, @ + 10, @ 0 THRU 100, @ 5600 K, GROUP 2, STORE GROUP 4, SCENE 5 and so on. Before ENTER, one line says what will happen (chapter 08).
  • A fixture now has one number, its Fixture Number. Unit No. and Show the Fixture Number in Settings are gone. The number is never empty; a fixture left without one gets the highest in use plus one (chapter 03).
  • Group names start with a number. A new group gets the next number, and RENUMBER in Group Order numbers them again (chapter 03).
  • In a fixture's panel on iPhone, Settings continue below LIGHT and the other contents; SETUP at the top is a shortcut there (chapters 05 and 06).
  • While a group master or the FREE master is down, the GM at the top of the screen gets a pulsing amber edge (chapter 04).
  • The Advanced heading in effects is now amber (chapter 09). In Settings → MIDI, Buttons and Keyboard start folded (chapter 12).
  • In a fixture's panel on iPad, NEXT, Delay, Fade and RESET sit on one line (chapter 08).

0.2 (357)

  • On iPad too, tapping a row in Fixture Sheet opens that fixture's panel (chapter 03).
  • The GRAND, FREE and group master faders no longer show the large number at the top of the screen; read the number above each fader (chapter 04).

0.2 (355)

  • ZEN on several fixtures now keeps their shape of levels. Take two at 100 and 50: raised from 0 they brighten in the same proportion and stop at 100 and 50. The panel for choosing what ZEN works on puts Fixtures first and narrows them by model or Home group (chapter 04).
  • Fire effects: Color Source now heads AUTO, COLOR and KEEP, with a line on what each means. The fires have no REPEAT and keep burning. In the Lights part of the effect list the fires come first. The waveform says PAUSED or RELEASED while the effect is paused or released (chapter 09).
  • LIGHTHOUSE joins the head movements, turning the light like a lighthouse (chapter 09).
  • Add in Patch no longer has an Offset field. Fixtures are spaced by the mode's channel count plus Gap (chapter 03).
  • Sending and the screen stay light with many fixtures patched and effects running.

0.2 (354)

  • Play now opens a list. Choose PLAY, ZEN, STAGE or FIXTURE SHEET. On iPad the rail on the left opens ZEN, STAGE and FIXTURE SHEET too. The Play row shows the current Scene's name at its top left (chapters 01 and 08).
  • A fixture panel now has the tabs LIGHT, MOVE, GRADIENT and SETUP. The names, Fade Time and the fixture settings are on SETUP (chapters 05 and 06).
  • Tapping GM lays out GRAND, FREE and the group masters side by side. BACK TO 100 under each puts it back, and the ✕ at the top left closes them. A lowered group's button shows its level, such as ↓60 (chapter 04).
  • ZEN in the Play list chooses what ZEN works on, and a ZEN group keeps faders ② and ③ (chapter 04). Tapping a row in Fixture Sheet opens that fixture's panel (chapter 03).
  • Taking one fixture out of BATTERY SAVE is now RELEASE, in a green band on its panel (chapters 06 and 10). A Scene's row shows two times, Fade and Delay (chapter 08).
  • Effects: TORCH, FIREPLACE and CAMPFIRE join the fires, and BONFIRE is now a large fire. DRAW takes up to four peaks. Effect colors can also be chosen from CCT, Gels and Favorites (chapter 09).
  • A show carries a copy of the MIDI, the output destination, the fade times and the Favorites. Choose Use or Keep when it opens (chapter 11).

0.2 (349)

  • On iPhone, Play steps through Scenes from Home. The bottom row turns into EXIT, UPDATE, BACK and NEXT (chapter 08).
  • Recalling a Scene no longer moves GM, B.O. or ⏻. Scenes do not store them. REVERT puts a Scene back to how it was when you recalled it, and FREE keeps a fixture out of recalls (chapter 08).
  • Group masters and the FREE master sit beside GM on iPhone (chapter 04). In Fixture Times, several fixtures drag together and the list narrows by model or group; the NEXT row in a fixture's panel sets its Delay and Fade into the next Scene (chapter 08).
  • Effects: ROLES for BEACON R/B, Describe to make one from words, CYCLE, and fires that redden as they dim. An effect on a locked fixture keeps running (chapters 06 and 09).
  • Slide to stop stops sending (chapter 02). MIDI can map UPDATE, SAVE and B.O., and a keyboard and Bluetooth MIDI work too (chapter 12).

0.2 (348)

  • EFFECT is the one way into effects. The Effects tab is gone: with nothing selected, EFFECT opens the list of what is running. Holding a round icon puts EFFECT beside ZEN (chapter 09).
  • New effects: NOD and SWEEP for the head, and DRAW, a shape you draw yourself. JUMP has Glide, and Shape works on EIGHT, BOX, SPIRAL and SEARCH (chapter 09).
  • Spread and Link set how far apart fixtures run or flicker, Energy moves a living effect's knobs together, TAP takes the beat, and In / Out fade an effect in and out (chapter 09).
  • The fluorescents are FLUO FLICKER and FLUO RESTART (chapter 09).
  • HISTORY has UNDO and REDO at the head of its list (chapter 10). On iPhone, UPDATE and RECORDING no longer appear at the top left (chapter 01).
  • A session can be joined from the iPhone's Camera app (chapter 13). Fixture Sheet has LIVE (chapter 03).
  • Heads that take no DMX of their own, such as the ARRI 650 Plus, have left the library: patch them under Tungsten, such as 650W (chapter 03).

0.2 (347)

  • Output starts off. Each time Kanau opens it sends nothing until you tap OUTPUT OFF at the top left and slide (chapter 02).
  • Kanau no longer sends over another sender on the same universe: it shows Blocked, with Join, Send … Only and Cancel. WAITING and Send anyway? are gone (chapter 02).
  • Output stops while Kanau is not on screen. SCREEN LOCK does not stop it (chapter 02).
  • LAMP MODE and Kanau Screen have six modes, four of them split into cells (chapters 02 and 03).
  • STAGE has no fade buttons any more; the six buttons are in each Scene's Settings → Fade (chapter 08).
  • A stored ★ color keeps the color temperature and G/M too (chapter 05).

0.2 (345)

  • A session is joined by QR code only. The guest scans the host's code, and works the light once the host taps Allow. Up to 8 guests can control at once (chapter 13).
  • Locks and limits belong to the console. No Scene records or applies them, so a recall never unlocks or re-limits a fixture (chapter 08).
  • Effects cross over with a Scene's fade instead of switching at the recall (chapter 08).
  • RENUMBER numbers every Scene 1, 2, 3 in list order, and a copy of 1 is named 1.1 (chapter 08).
  • COLOR works on what you select, down to single pixels, and opens for any selection (chapter 05).
  • GM sits at the right end of the status line. On iPhone, BLIND puts UPDATE in the place of BATTERY SAVE (chapter 01).

0.2 (341)

  • LAMP MODE turns an iPhone or iPad into a light that another console drives (chapter 02).
  • A Scene has a Delay and a Curve: S-CURVE, EASE IN or LINEAR. Each fixture's Delay counts from GO (chapter 08).
  • What you touch during a fade leaves it and is recorded into the Scene the fade is heading for (chapter 08).
  • A universe switched OFF is no longer sent at all (chapter 02).
  • The fluorescents are now FLUO FLICKER, FLUO DROPOUT, FLUO RESTART and FLUO DYING (chapter 09).
  • × closes a panel from the top left.

QUICK START — try Kanau in 3 minutes

The first time Kanau opens, a practice rig of 4 fixtures is already patched. You do not need a single light to try the three steps below. They take about three minutes.

Button names are written exactly as they appear on screen.

1. Change the intensity

  1. Drag a fader up and down. The number above it and the color of the round icon change with it.
  2. Tap GM at the top right of the screen (GM 100 on iPad). In the panel that opens, pull down the GRAND fader at the right end, and everything gets dimmer. The band at the top of the screen and the edge of the screen turn red.
  3. Tap BACK TO 100 to bring the brightness back, and close the panel with the × at the top left.

A fader moves by the distance your finger travels, not the place you touched. Where you start makes no difference to the result.

2. Change the color

  1. Press and hold the round icon above a fader. The color panel opens.
  2. Intensity sets brightness; the color picker and the R, G, B bars set color. A fixture with color temperature also shows Color Temperature.
  3. The ‹ › at the top move you to the previous or next fixture.

The items in the panel depend on what the fixture can do.

3. Recall a Scene

  1. Open the Scenes tab at the bottom. It holds four Scenes: DIM, COLOR, PIXELS, FX.
  2. Tap one of them.
  3. Close the panel with × at the top left. On Home, the faders and colors have changed to that Scene.
  4. On iPhone, tap Play at the bottom, then PLAY in the list that opens. The bottom row turns into BACK and NEXT, so you can step through the Scenes while you watch Home. EXIT brings the tabs back.

With the starting setting (AUTO UPDATE), changing intensity or color after a recall rewrites that Scene. To keep a Scene as it is, see chapter 08.

See the values going out

Even with no lights attached, you can see the DMX values Kanau sends.

  1. Tap OUTPUT OFF at the top left. A Slide to send row opens below it.
  2. Slide the round handle all the way to the right. Sending starts (chapter 02).
  3. Open Settings → DMX Monitor. It shows the numbers Kanau is actually sending.

The numbers in DMX Monitor change as soon as you move a fader.

The demo fixtures are patched on U1 from address 1. Do not start sending the demo on a network that reaches real lights.

What is in the practice rig

The demo you get on first launch holds the following.

  • Fixtures: 4 from Generic: three RGBW and one BAR (4 pixels).
  • Groups: three: KEY (two RGBW), BACK (one RGBW) and FLOOR (the BAR).
  • Scenes: four are saved: DIM, COLOR, PIXELS and FX.
  • Effect: FLOOR has a fire effect running.
  • BATTERY SAVE: two fixtures are marked for it, one RGBW and the BAR. Their numbers have a green background.
  • GM: 100.

None of these fixtures is a real product. They are there so you can try the controls and watch the values change in DMX Monitor.

Connecting real lights

Once the demo makes sense, move to your own gear.

  1. Prepare with output off: leave OUTPUT OFF as it is and make a new show with Settings → Shows → New Show. The demo fixtures are patched on U1 from address 1, so sending the demo can reach the lights on site.
  2. Patch: Patch → ＋ Fixtures → Add New Fixture, then set the model, DMX mode, universe and address. Make them the same as the settings on the fixture itself (chapter 03).
  3. Join the network: put the iPhone on the same network as your DMX node.
  4. Check the node: in Settings → Output, check that Nodes Answering is 1 or more. Gear that does not answer polling stays at 0 while receiving normally. If yours stays at 0, carry on anyway and judge by the light itself.
  5. Start sending: first check where the faders are on Home, and the Universes in Settings → Output (the universes that will go out). Then tap OUTPUT OFF at the top left of Home and slide the round handle all the way to the right. Once sending starts, Network Output in Settings → Output shows a figure (chapter 02).
  6. Build the look: set intensity and color on Home (chapters 04 and 05).
  7. Save it: tap SAVE in Scenes to store the look (chapter 08).

The practice rig is an ordinary show. Once your own lights are patched, you can delete the demo show.

Five things worth knowing first

  1. Fixture Lock beats blackout. A locked fixture stays lit through B.O. (chapter 10).
  2. Under AUTO UPDATE a recalled Scene records what you do. Switch to MANUAL UPDATE, or lock it, to leave it alone (chapter 08). Recalling a Scene never moves the grand master, B.O. or a fixture's power.
  3. There are three kinds of lock. Fixture Lock holds the output, Scene Lock protects what a Scene has stored, SCREEN LOCK stops stray touches (chapter 10). Hanging the iPhone upside down also locks the screen (Strap Lock); slide right to unlock.
  4. When the grand master is below 100, the band at the top of the screen turns red and the edge of the screen pulses red. If things look dim, look at the color of the top band and the edge first.
  5. Output is off every time Kanau opens. To start sending, tap OUTPUT OFF at the top left and slide the round handle. To stop, tap the same place and slide the handle in Slide to stop. When another console is sending on the same universe, you will see Blocked or SHARED (chapter 02).
WARNING

A fixture with Lock on will not go out when you press B.O., and will not go out when you pull the grand master to zero. Check that your locks are clear before a take. The count of what is still lit during a blackout is shown next to the green 🔒 at the top of the screen.

Where everything is on the Home screen. The meaning of each color and mark is collected here too.

Learn these eight first

Before the detailed tables, these are the only places you need to know.

Everything below is the detail.

The tabs at the bottom

Home is where you work. Tapping a tab at the bottom opens a panel or a list over Home.

  • Scenes, Patch, Settings: a panel opens over Home.
  • Play on iPhone: a list of PLAY, COMMAND, ZEN, STAGE and FIXTURE SHEET opens. Tapping PLAY in the list opens no panel; it turns the bottom row into the Play row.
  • Play on iPad: it sits in the column on the left. It opens a list of COMMAND, ZEN, STAGE and FIXTURE SHEET. There is no PLAY.

To come back to Home, drag the handle at the top of the panel down, or tap × at the top left. A panel opened from inside another one, such as DMX Monitor, has ‹ at the top left instead of ×. Tapping ‹ goes back one panel.

Some things differ by device and situation.

  • A device that has joined a session has no Patch.
  • On iPad with iPadOS 18 or later, the panels almost fill the screen. COLOR, EFFECT, Patch and Scenes are laid out in two columns when the window is wide enough.

The status line

The left of the status line is the send state. Tap it to open the row that starts and stops sending (chapter 02). Each time Kanau opens it reads OUTPUT OFF, and nothing goes out until you slide.

While sending it reads SENDING and the universes, such as SENDING U1 U2. Where there is no room, it becomes a single letter for the route. Art-Net is A, sACN is S.

The dot next to it pulses while sending, while waiting for the slide, and while LISTENING. Bluetooth has its own dot and name.

Next to them is the name of the show that is open. On a narrow phone, where the row has no room to spare, it is left out.

While BLIND is on, this whole left part becomes an amber BLIND. Tap it to leave BLIND (chapter 08).

ShownMeaning
OUTPUT OFFNothing has been sent since Kanau opened. Tap it to open the Slide to send row below, then slide. If you change the look while nothing is sent, it turns red and reads Not sent, and stays red until you start sending
SENDING, tappedOpens Slide to stop. Slide right to stop sending; the line goes back to OUTPUT OFF. Done closes the row
LISTENINGChecking for another sender before sending, for about a second
SENDING U1 U2Those universes are going out. A gray U3 OFF here is a universe that has fixtures patched but has not been slid to start sending yet. It is not the red U1 OFF further right on the line
Blocked U1Another sender is already on that universe, so Kanau does not send on it. Tap it for the choices (chapter 02)
Green dotSending
Amber dotSlowed down, or reconnecting (Reconnecting…)
Red dot, ART-NET No node or SACN No nodeNo node is answering. Tap it to open Settings → Output. While the Play row is showing it does not open, so tap EXIT first. The route's name is shortened on a narrow screen
Red dot, ART-NET Blocked or SACN BlockedSending has stopped for a reason that will not clear by itself. Tap it to open Settings → Output, which shows the reason and what to do about it in red. The route's name and Blocked are shortened on a narrow screen
Gray dot, IdleSending has been started but nothing is going out. Shown when every universe is switched off, or when there is no network
SHARED and an IP or a device nameAnother console is sending to the same universe. This one is still sending too
JOINED or WATCH ONLY, and a nameIn a session. DMX goes out from the host
FREE ×3 (white)How many fixtures are FREE. Shown now and then in place of the send state (chapter 08)

SENDING and a green dot do not prove the light received anything. Chapter 02 explains how to check the connection; chapter 14 covers what to do, symptom by symptom.

The middle and right of the line carry these. GM sits at the right end, after SCREEN LOCK.

ItemTapHold, or note
GM 100Opens the grand master panelHold for its settings. Below 100 it is filled red and pulses
B.O.Clears the blackout. At GM 0 it opens the GM panel insteadReplaces GM while the console is dark. B.O. is also shown when GM is 0
U1 OFF (red)NothingWhich universes are switched off, by number. Up to three, then + for more. Turn them back on in Settings → Output
🔒 n (green)NothingWhat is still lit while the console is dark: locked fixtures, faders set as a switch that are ON (when the grand master is at 0), and locks left at an old address
BATTERY SAVETurns it on and offHold to set the brightness and the fade time. While it is on, it now and then shows the brightness the fixtures keep, such as 50%
SCREEN LOCKDoes not lockHold for 0.5 seconds to lock the screen

Notes on the table:

  • GM: on iPhone it reads GM, or just the number when it is down. While a group master or the FREE master is down, its edge pulses amber.
  • U1 OFF and 🔒: they appear only when needed. U1 OFF appears when a universe with fixtures patched is switched off. 🔒 appears while the console is dark (a blackout, or the grand master at 0).
  • UPDATE: on iPhone, while BLIND is on, UPDATE takes the place of BATTERY SAVE. Tapping it records the BLIND look into the current Scene (chapter 08). While the Play row is showing, UPDATE is in the Play row instead.
  • Strap Lock: when it is on, hanging the iPhone upside down also locks the screen. Slide right to unlock it.

Fixtures / GroupsSwitches between showing by model and showing by group. On iPad it sits in the status row at the top of Home
10 / 5Faders on a page. Five makes each one wider. On iPad it is 30 / 20 / 15 (40 / 20 on a 13-inch), in the status row
HISTORYOpens the list of earlier states, with UNDO ↓ and REDO ↑ at its head. On iPhone it sits at the right end of the Fixtures / Groups row; on iPad, in the status row just left of GM
Model and group buttonsTap to show those fixtures on Home. Hold to set color and intensity for all of them. What is written on a button is explained below the table
CLEAR nClears the selection. The light does not change
‹ / ›Moves between pages. While the FREE master is down, this row shows its level, such as FREE ↓0 (chapter 04)
NumberIntensity from 0 to 100. Shown large at the top while you drag
Round fixture icon (…)Tap to select. Hold to open that fixture's panel
FaderDrag up and down to set intensity
Model nameMarks a run of the same model and mode
Number buttonThe fixture number. In piano mode it changes intensity while held
⏻Turns the output off and on, keeping the value
COLORSets color and intensity for the selected fixtures
EFFECTApplies an effect to the selected fixtures. With nothing selected, opens the list of running effects
PIXELSOpens and closes the cells of pixel fixtures
Play rowOn iPhone, shown after you tap Play → PLAY. EXIT brings back the usual buttons (chapter 08)
＋ −Cycles piano mode: LOCK → ＋ → −
FINECycles sensitivity: normal → FINE (1/10) → FINE+ (1/20)

A model or group button carries the following.

  • Fixture count: after the name, such as ×24.
  • Mode mark: when two buttons would carry the same name, a mark such as [111] sits between the name and the count.
  • Group master level: while the master is down, its level follows, such as ↓60. An unselected button's edge slowly pulses (chapter 04).

COLOR, EFFECT and PIXELS each have their own condition.

  • COLOR: unavailable with no fixture selected. With a selection it opens, even for fixtures with no color (chapter 05).
  • EFFECT: always opens. With a selection it opens the effect panel for those fixtures; with none, the list of running effects (chapter 09).
  • PIXELS: unavailable when no fixture on the page has pixels.

Colors and marks

Color or markMeaning
AmberSelected, or active
RedBlackout, a low grand master, a network problem, piano mode. Something to check
GreenSending. Fixture Lock. BATTERY SAVE on
Amber band and edgeBLIND is on. What you do does not reach the lights
PurpleOutput switched off, or the screen locked
CyanBeing worked by the other device in a session
OrangeAt a limit you set
GrayUnavailable, or stopped

Tap the round icon to select the fixture; hold it to open the fixture's panel. The icon carries the fixture's color and its real output:

  • Color: it never shows a color the fixture cannot send, so a dimmer-only fixture shows white. A color that gives no light, such as RGB all at 0, draws the circle as off even when the intensity is above 0.
  • Pixels: it reads the cells as well, so a fixture at 100 with every cell down shows dark. When the cells differ in color or intensity, the circle splits into one wedge per cell, cell 1 at twelve o'clock and the rest clockwise; with up to four cells, thin lines divide the wedges. When every cell is the same, it stays one circle.
  • Rims and marks: a selection shows an amber rim, a switched-off output a purple ring and ⏻, a lock a green outer ring and 🔒, a FREE fixture an F.
  • Effects: a running effect makes it move.

The edge of the screen shows that the output is being held down. The status line shows what is holding it down.

EdgeMeaning
Red, pulsing, with a light traveling around itThe grand master is below 100
Thicker, deeper red, with a faster lightThe grand master is at 0, or a blackout
Green, with a long light sliding slowly around itBATTERY SAVE is on
Red and green taking turnsBoth: red for about six seconds, green for about three
Amber frame, joined to the band at the top where the clock isBLIND is on. A low grand master pulses red on the frame; green is not shown

02 Sending DMX — Output

Setting up the link to your lighting gear, and checking that DMX is getting there.

First connection

One Art-Net node

  1. Put the iPhone on the same Wi-Fi or wired network as the node.
  2. Open Settings → Output.
  3. Choose Art-Net and AUTO. Both are the defaults.
  4. Check that Nodes Answering is 1 or more. Some gear never answers polling and stays at 0 while it is receiving normally, so do not stop here if the figure will not move.
  5. On Home, tap OUTPUT OFF at the top left. A row opens under the status line; slide the round handle of Slide to send all the way to the right.
  6. The status line reads LISTENING for about a second, then SENDING U1, and Network Output shows a figure in packets/s. Move a fader and watch the light respond.

Kanau never starts sending by itself. Each time it opens, output is off and the status line reads OUTPUT OFF; the patch, the destination and the switched-off universes are kept. Moving a fader or recalling a Scene never starts output.

If the light changes while nothing is being sent, the status at the top left turns red and reads OUTPUT OFF / Not sent, and stays red until you start sending. The first time you touch a fader while nothing is being sent, the row above the faders turns red and reads Not sent / Slide OUTPUT to send, and goes back 2 seconds after you lift your finger. That row appears only once while output is off. There is no vibration.

When you slide, Kanau first listens for about a second for another sender. It then sends every patched, switched-on universe that has no other sender on it, continuously. The rate is normally 44 Hz. Bluetooth connects when you slide, not at launch.

To stop sending, tap the status line and slide Slide to stop to the right. It goes back to OUTPUT OFF.

Output also goes back to off, and you have to slide again, when:

  • you change between Art-Net and sACN
  • a network appears that was not there when you slid
  • you leave a session as a guest
  • you leave LITE MODE

A universe added to the patch later stays off until you slide, and the status line shows it, for example, as U3 OFF. Output stops while Kanau is not on screen and starts again when you come back; SCREEN LOCK does not stop it.

Is it sending?

Read these in order. Each one tells you something different, and none of them can tell you that the light itself received the data.

WhereWhat it tells you
The dot on the status lineKanau is sending, or is about to (chapter 01)
Network Output in Settings → OutputHow many packets went out over the network in the last second. A figure in packets/s means Kanau is sending; Nothing means it is not
Nodes Answering in Settings → OutputWhich nodes answered Kanau. Gear that does not answer polling shows 0 while it is receiving
Settings → DMX MonitorThe values Kanau is sending, channel by channel

Settings in detail

Protocol and networks

Art-Net and sACN are exclusive: pick one. CRMX over Bluetooth runs alongside either.

Network lists your Wi-Fi, Ethernet and Hotspot connections with their addresses and how many nodes answered on each.

  • By default it uses every network available.
  • From the all-selected state, tapping one leaves only that one on. After that each tap turns one on or off.
  • With only one network, tapping it stops network output, and tapping it again goes back to using it.
  • Turn them all off and nothing goes out over the network. Bluetooth keeps sending.
  • A connection marked No address cannot be selected.

If you use wired and Wi-Fi together, check that both appear in the list.

Choosing the destination

SettingWhere it sendsWhen to use it
AUTO (Art-Net)To the nodes that answered; broadcast when none answersThe normal choice
BROADCAST (Art-Net)Every frame to each network's subnetWhen a node reports a wrong address and nothing arrives on AUTO
UNICASTStraight to the addresses you enterWhen broadcast does not reach the node, or you want to name the target
255.255.255.255 (Art-Net)Broadcast on the segment. Does not cross a routerWhen addressing does not line up and ordinary broadcast fails. iOS may block it
MULTICAST (sACN)The multicast address for each universeThe sACN default

On AUTO, where each universe goes depends on what the nodes answer.

  • A universe that a node lists in its reply: goes by unicast to those nodes.
  • A node that lists no universes: gets them all.
  • A universe no node lists: is broadcast every frame. It is not broadcast when an address is ticked in the list below.

When a node starts answering for a universe that was being broadcast, from then on that universe goes only to the nodes that answer. An amber notice on Home says so. Gear that does not answer then needs its address typed into the list.

With UNICAST, type the node's address and tap Add. The same list is shown under AUTO, for gear that does not answer polling.

  • A ticked address: every universe goes to it.
  • An unticked address: it stays in the list but nothing is sent to it. The box is at the left of the address.
  • ×: removes the address from the list.

With UNICAST and nothing ticked, a red line says No node IP is switched on or entered. No DMX is going out over the network.

If Nodes Answering is 1 or more on AUTO but a light does not respond, check whether the node is reporting the wrong address for itself. Look at Destination and try BROADCAST. Chapter 14 covers the other causes.

RESCAN

Tapping RESCAN under Art-Net refreshes the node list. Use it after adding gear, removing gear or changing an address. Left alone, a new node appears within about 3 seconds. A removed one disappears after about 10 seconds.

Sending continues while it scans. RESCAN also measures the round trip to each node that answers. RESCAN is unavailable with no usable network.

When the output stops

In Settings → Output, a red line says what stopped the output and what to do about it. It says things such as these.

  • Turn on the local network permission
  • Switch to UNICAST and type the node's address
  • Check the address you typed
  • Check the Wi-Fi
  • Give the node power

CRMX carries a line of its own. The console's own wording stays in brackets at the end, so it can be quoted exactly.

Universes and Art-Net numbering

Universes lists each patched universe with its fixture count, how many are lit, and an ON/OFF switch. A universe that is OFF reads Not sending, and so does one that has not been slid since it was patched.

IMPORTANT

OFF stops sending that universe. Nothing goes out for it on Art-Net or sACN, and over Bluetooth the link stays up but nothing is written. A receiver may keep its last values, so a light can stay lit. The top of the screen names the universes that are switched off, such as U1 OFF.

Use Net / Sub / Uni only when your node asks for Net / Sub-Net / Universe instead of a single number. Turn it on in Settings → Output → Art-Net → Net / Sub / Uni. The relationship is Net × 256 + Sub × 16 + Uni.

With it on and the route on Art-Net, patching takes the universe the same way.

  • Add, Re-address and Re-patch show Net (0–127), Sub (0–15) and Uni (0–15) to type.
  • The universe they make, such as U500, is shown beside them.
  • A number beyond its range is set to the end of the range.

sACN priority can be 0, 100 or 200. It is 100 by default, and it is the priority Kanau sends with its sACN output.

CRMX over Bluetooth

  1. Turn on Bluetooth in Settings → Output → CRMX (Bluetooth).
  2. Allow Bluetooth the first time iOS asks.
  3. Pick a transmitter from the list. Tapping it again disconnects.

The transmitter you pick carries the universe your patch uses (U1 when the patch sits in universe 1). Next time, turning Bluetooth on reconnects to the same one, once you have slid to send. When a transmitter cannot connect or drops out, Settings → Output says what to check, with the system's own message in brackets.

  • The list: it says connected for a transmitter that is linked and sending for one that is receiving data.
  • When the patch spans more than one universe: choose which one it carries with − and + on the Universe row under the transmitter. Once you choose by hand, Kanau stops choosing for you until you disconnect the transmitter and pick it again.
  • A second transmitter: scanning stops once the ones you picked are connected, so RESCAN is how you look for another one.

With the same universe going out over both the network and Bluetooth, Settings → Output says so: U1: network and Bluetooth output are both on. That is a statement of fact, not a warning.

A CRMX receiver takes the output of the transmitter it is linked to. The same U1 on Kanau does not by itself feed one fixture twice.

Flicker only happens where a fixture really is receiving from both paths. Stop one of them there.

If a transmitter still refuses Art-Net after you turn Bluetooth off, check the transmitter's own settings.

When another console is found

ShownWhat it means, and what to do
Blocked U1When you slid, another console was already sending Art-Net on U1, so Kanau does not send on it. Tap it for the choices below. You cannot override the other sender
SHARED + IP or a device nameAnother console appeared after this one started. Sending continues, so stop one of them if you need to

Tapping Blocked U1 opens a row that names the sender, such as U1 In Use, with these choices:

ChoiceWhat it does
JoinShown when the sender is a Kanau host. Opens Session to join it
Send U2 OnlyShown when other universes are free. Sends only those
CancelCloses the row without sending

Kanau devices tell each other which universes they send, so two that slide at once do not both send. An sACN sender is shown in red in the send row, by name or IP. This is for information only: the universe is not Blocked, and Kanau keeps sending. Unicast senders and Bluetooth in other apps may not be detected.

LITE MODE — this device as a light

LITE MODE turns this iPhone or iPad into a light that another console drives over Art-Net or sACN. It is not offered while BLIND is on.

  1. Open Settings → LITE MODE, the last folding heading, just above DMX Monitor.
  2. Choose a MODE from the list (see the table below the steps). The number at the start of a name is the mode number. It starts on 2: SCREEN RGB 9ch. 1: BACK LIGHT ONLY is not listed on a device with no back light, but the other modes keep their numbers.
  3. Choose Art-Net or sACN.
  4. Set Universe and Address, by typing them or with − and +. The line under them shows which addresses each part takes.
  5. On a device with a proximity sensor, PROXIMITY appears below. When it is on, the screen goes dark while you hold this device to your ear. The back light and vibration keep going. It starts off.
  6. To show images or videos, add them to Media first (see below).
  7. Tap LITE MODE START.

The modes to choose from in step 2 are 1: BACK LIGHT ONLY 1ch and those in this table.

RGBHUE SAT
2: SCREEN RGB 9ch3: SCREEN HUE SAT 8ch
4: SCREEN 2 CELLS RGB 17ch5: SCREEN 2 CELLS HUE SAT 15ch
6: SCREEN 4 CELLS RGB 31ch7: SCREEN 4 CELLS HUE SAT 27ch
8: SCREEN 8 CELLS RGB 59ch9: SCREEN 8 CELLS HUE SAT 51ch
10: SCREEN 4 STRIPS RGB 31ch11: SCREEN 4 STRIPS HUE SAT 27ch
12: SCREEN 8 STRIPS RGB 59ch13: SCREEN 8 STRIPS HUE SAT 51ch
14: SCREEN FX & MEDIA RGB 18ch15: SCREEN FX & MEDIA HUE SAT 17ch
16: SCREEN COOKIE RGB 62ch17: SCREEN COOKIE HUE SAT 54ch
18: ULTIMATE RGB 72ch19: ULTIMATE HUE SAT 64ch

The screen reads WAITING until the first data arrives, then turns the color it receives; if the data stops, it keeps the last color.

BACK LIGHT ONLY uses only the light on the back, with one channel, Back Light. The screen stays dark.

The other modes start with Screen Dimmer and end with Back Light and Vibration. What comes between them depends on the mode.

  • SCREEN RGB: CCT, G/M, Crossfade, Red, Green and Blue.
  • SCREEN HUE SAT: CCT, G/M, Crossfade, Hue and Saturation.
  • CELLS: the screen is split into 2, 4 or 8 parts, each with its own Dimmer, CCT, G/M, Crossfade and color. They are numbered from the top left. Eight parts are 2 columns by 4 rows on an upright screen and 4 columns by 2 rows on a sideways one.
  • STRIPS: the screen is split into 4 or 8 strips along its long side. Each strip has the same channels as a cell. They are numbered from the top on an upright screen and from the left on a sideways one.
  • SCREEN FX & MEDIA: the whole screen is one part. After the color come Color Macro, Content, Speed, Amount, Size, Mix, Media, Playback and Color Temp, which put moving patterns on the screen.
  • SCREEN COOKIE: the screen is split into irregular, dappled areas, painted with the colors of 8 cells.
  • ULTIMATE: Cells chooses how the screen is split (SCREEN, CELLS, STRIPS or COOKIE), and the patterns of FX & MEDIA are there too.

Each channel works as follows.

  • Crossfade: the share of white and color. 0 is white and 255 is color. While it is at 0, moving the Red, Green and Blue faders leaves the screen white. Choosing a color with the color picker or from the gel list moves Crossfade too.
  • CCT and G/M: set the white. CCT runs from 1750 to 9910 K.
  • Hue: 0 to 255 covers the whole circle.
  • Screen Dimmer: dims the screen only.
  • Back Light and Vibration: the light on the back of the device, and its vibration. A device without one leaves it out.

Tap Media to open a list of numbers, 1 to 51, that hold images and videos.

  • Adding: tap a number and choose Add from Photos or Add from Files to add one from the Photos app or from a file.
  • A number that holds one: Replace from Photos and Replace from Files swap it, Move to moves it to another number, and Delete removes it.
  • How a number is picked: the Media channel on the other console picks the number. 1–5 is 1, 6–10 is 2, and so on.
  • Where they appear: on the screen in the FX & MEDIA and ULTIMATE modes.

The files stay on this device.

On the other console, patch it as Kanau Lite (chapter 03). On Art-Net it answers polling as Kanau Lite, so it appears under that name in the other console's list of nodes.

To leave, slide the switch at the top right across, then tap the × that appears. While LITE MODE is on, this device sends no DMX, MIDI is off, the screen is at full brightness and does not lock itself, and a guest leaves its session. Leaving puts the brightness and MIDI back, with output off again.

Kanau Lite is a free, separate app that turns a device into a light in the same way. The values of each FX & MEDIA, COOKIE and ULTIMATE channel, and how Kanau Lite differs from LITE MODE, are on the Kanau Lite page.

DMX Diagnostics — reading what is happening

The lower half of Output is there to show you where things stopped. It is not a set of settings. When output is slow or missing, read it from the top (chapter 14).

ItemHow to read it
DestinationWhere it is really going. ↦ after an address means unicast to a node that answered
MediumThe connections in use, for example Wi-Fi + Ethernet
Network OutputPackets sent over the network in the last second. Bluetooth is not counted here (see below the table)
ClockThe worst gap between sends. About 23 ms is normal. Over 100 ms points at the phone
Touch → DMXFrom your finger to the packet. About 25 ms is normal
Nodes AnsweringHow many answered, with name, address, connection and round trip (see below the table)
Type these into the nodeThe Net / Sub / Uni to enter on the node, when that display is on

Notes on the table:

  • Network Output: around 44 is normal for one universe to one destination. It multiplies with each extra universe or destination. Nothing means none went out, as before you slide.
  • Nodes Answering: the round trip is blank until RESCAN measures it. The figure in brackets is the worst of the last 10 seconds. On AUTO, the line under each node lists the universes sent to it, such as U1 or U0–U3.

These narrow the problem down; they do not prove success. They are what Kanau sent, and whether the light received it cannot be seen from here. Network Output can show a figure while a mismatch or a fault at the other end keeps the lights dark. Gear that does not answer polling shows 0 under Nodes Answering even while it is receiving.

DMX Monitor

Settings → DMX Monitor shows all 512 channels of each universe as they go out. It refreshes 10 times a second. Reading it does not affect sending. A universe that is not going out, because it is OFF or has not been slid open, shows its heading with OFF and no values.

The cells only show values; nothing can be typed here. A lock whose fixture has been deleted is listed above the grid, with UNLOCK.

The values read as percent or as raw DMX, following the same setting as the rest of the console.

With more than one universe, a Universe pulldown sits beside the unit button. Choosing one opens that universe and jumps to its start.

Each universe can be folded separately. A folded heading still shows its count of active channels, so you can see which one is busy without opening it.

  • Nothing arrives, or it is slow → chapter 14

03 Patching fixtures — Patch

Register the lights you are using, and set the model, DMX mode, universe, address, number and groups.

Intensity and color are set on Home (chapters 04 and 05).

Adding fixtures

At the top of Patch, Fixtures | Groups switches between the fixtures and the groups. ＋ Fixtures and ＋ Group always sit at the top of their side. On iPad, where Patch has two columns, both sides show at once.

  1. Open Patch → ＋ Fixtures and tap Add New Fixture to show the fields.
  2. Choose Manufacturer → Fixture → Mode. The mode must match the one set on the fixture itself. Each of the three opens as a list of its own with a search field, so a long list of models is a matter of typing rather than scrolling.
  3. Set how many, the universe and the start address.
  4. Check the range and any warnings, then tap Add. It is saved as it is added.

Most of the time, Manufacturer, Fixture, Mode, How Many and Universe / Address are all you need to set.

FieldWhat it is
FavoritesWhere modes and manufacturers are starred. Tap a ★ to add or remove a favorite (see below the table)
NameThis fixture's own name. It appears in Patch and the Patch List. Defaults to the full model name plus a running number, such as Titan Tube 1. The name under the faders is separate (see below the table)
Number / How ManyThe fixture's number (its Fixture Number), and how many to add, up to 4,096. Leave the number empty and the fixtures are numbered for you, from the highest in use plus one
LabelThe display name shared by every fixture of that model in the same mode. It runs under the faders. Defaults to the official model name (see below the table)
Universe / AddressThe universe and start address. Defaults to U1 and the next free address. U0 is allowed (see below the table)
GapEmpty channels left between fixtures. A short note beside the field says so
BATTERY SAVEMarks the new fixtures for BATTERY SAVE
Label ColorThe background of the number. Seven colors, or none
MapThe 512-channel layout. Drag and release to set the start address (see below the table)
TOGETHER / FILL GAPSThe pulldown left of Add. Chooses how the new fixtures are placed (see below the table)

Notes on the table:

  • Favorites: a ★ sits beside each mode, the Mode field and each manufacturer. Starred modes appear as buttons under Favorites, and starred manufacturers go to the top of the list. Edit beside Favorites lists them all.
  • Name: the name under the faders is set by Label and Name (chapter 06).
  • Label: change Mode here and a Label you have not typed follows the new mode. It can also be typed in the fixture's panel (chapter 06).
  • Universe / Address: changing the universe resets the address to 1. The line below shows the free space from the address you typed, as in Free: 1 – 512 (512 ch). It reads Does not fit in amber if the fixtures will not fit there, and Free: None if nothing is free.
  • Map: the Universe pulldown above it shows how much of each universe is in use, as in U46 · 2 / 512. Choosing one moves there, and the start address becomes the first free space that holds every fixture you are adding.
  • TOGETHER: places every fixture in one run. The form goes back to TOGETHER each time it opens.
  • FILL GAPS: puts each fixture into the next free space from Address on, and what does not fit goes into free space in the next universe. The place you choose is where the search starts, so Does not fit does not appear.

Each fixture after the first starts at the previous start address plus the mode's channel count and Gap. The addresses do not overlap.

  • The step: the line under the form shows it, such as (16 ch step).
  • Anything past 512: goes into the first free space in the next universe that holds all the rest.
  • When FILL GAPS scatters the fixtures: the line shows the first and last, as in U1 1 → U1 203 (5 × 4 ch).

Afterwards a panel lists what went in, one row per fixture, with its number, name and address. At its head is a line like Added 3 × Titan Tube — U1 1–15. When the places are not in one run, it shows the first and last address, as in U1 1 → U1 203. It stays until you tap OK, so you can keep patching and read it afterwards.

Patched, under the form, lists the models already patched. Tap a row to open the form with that model and mode filled in.

The fixture number

A fixture has one number, its Fixture Number. Home's number buttons, the panel title, Fixture Sheet, Labels and command entry (chapter 08) all use that same number.

The number is never empty. A fixture patched with the number left empty, a fixture whose number you clear, and a fixture in an older show without one are numbered from the highest in use plus one, with three digits such as 001. Gaps are not filled. Giving two fixtures the same number raises a warning but is allowed.

Models and modes

This version ships with 61 manufacturers, 1,062 fixtures and 15,454 modes. For anything not in the library, use the Generic definitions or Custom Fixtures.

Three manufacturers in the list are not makers of lights:

ManufacturerWhat it holds
GenericDimmer, Dimmer 16-bit, Bi-color, CCT, RGB, RGBW, Dimmer + RGB and Dimmer + RGBW
Tungsten40 one-channel lights that dim warm, worked through a dimmer (see below the table)
KanauKanau Lite, a device in LITE MODE (chapter 02; see below the table)

Notes on the table:

  • Tungsten: it holds household ones such as Bulb, Desk lamp and Practical, sizes from 150W to 20kW, trade names such as Tweenie, Baby, Junior and Redhead, Par 64, Fresnel, and Switch, the one that does not dim. An ARRI 650 Plus, for example, is the 650W, in mode 1ch · D.
  • How many fixtures Kanau patches: one Add patches three fixtures in a row: Kanau Lite, Kanau Back Light and Kanau Vibration. BACK LIGHT ONLY patches one fixture, Kanau Back Light. The patched fixtures are named like Lite 1, Back 1 and Vibe 1.
  • Kanau's modes: any of the 19 modes of LITE MODE. The number at the start of a mode's name is the mode number, and the number at the end is the number of channels the three take together. The CELLS, STRIPS, COOKIE and ULTIMATE modes split the screen into pixels, opened with PIXELS. In ULTIMATE, the faders of cells that are not on the Kanau Lite screen are dimmed. A dimmed fader still works.
  • Kanau under Channels: the Cells, Color Macro, Content, Media and Playback rows read as the name you chose, not as a percent. The Playback row has 3 buttons: play, pause and restart. The Media row has an arrow button on each side.

There are also the following kinds of mode.

  • PROVISIONAL (Advanced): a placeholder mode, used where the DMX chart has not been worked through. It sends intensity on channel 1 and nothing else.
  • Modes with no dimmer channel: the fader drives the color channels together, acting as a virtual dimmer.

Changing patched fixtures

Patched lists fixtures by model and mode. Tap a heading to fold it.

  • Order: inside a model, and in the All row, the fixtures follow the order of the faders on Home (chapter 04).
  • A model's row: shows its addresses as U1 1–9 when they run on, or as the first and last, as in U1 1 → U1 203, when they do not.
  • A fixture's row: tap it to open its patch settings.

Patch List, under the Patched heading, shows every patched fixture in address order, universe by universe. It is there to read while you set addresses on the fixtures themselves; nothing in it can be changed.

  • Each row: shows the universe and start address in large type, with the end address under them, the fixture's number, then its name and mode. Modes are never cut short.
  • An overlapping fixture: on both fixtures that overlap, the start address is red and marked ⚠.
  • Export PDF: at the top right. It makes an A4 copy to hand out, with the show name and the date on each page.

⚠ marks any of these.

  • A fixture with an overlapping address
  • A fixture that runs past channel 512
  • A fixture whose output is being held at other values by a lock. Open the fixture to see it.

Sending continues while it is showing, so check the settings.

Two fixtures on overlapping addresses can both be used. An overlapping address sends the value of the fixture you moved last. On Home, a fixture that overlaps carries a red ! above its value.

n fixture data problems refers to faults found while loading fixture data. Tap it for details.

Working in the Patched list does not change which fixtures Home is showing.

Fixture Sheet and Labels

Both are in Settings, below DMX Monitor. Fixture Sheet also opens from FIXTURE SHEET in the Play list. Opening either one does not change the show. Fixture Sheet is not available on a device that has joined a session, or while BLIND is on.

Fixture Sheet shows the current state of every fixture, in the order of All on Home: number and name, address, intensity, color, any running effect, and marks such as LOCK and OFF. Tap a row to open the same panel you get by holding that fixture's round icon (intensity, color, effect and setup), and adjust it there.

  • ALL | LIVE ONLY, first under the title: LIVE ONLY keeps only the fixtures that are lit now and those running an effect. With nothing lit the list reads Nothing is lit. % | DMX, at the right of the same row, shows the values as percentages or as raw DMX values.
  • The row under it narrows the list further without changing Home. Fixtures | Groups at its left switches between model buttons and ALL with a button for each group, as on Home.
  • Export PDF takes what the list shows, and asks whether to take a group or everything.

Labels, in Settings below Fixture Sheet, makes stickers for the fixtures as an A4 PDF, in address order.

  • Standard: 52.5 × 37.125 mm, 32 to a sheet.
  • Small: 26.25 × 14.85 mm, 160 to a sheet.
  • Copies: sets 1 to 4 per fixture.
  • What a label carries: the fixture number, the Label, the start address and the mode.

Under the preview, Page 1 of 3 says how many sheets there are, and ‹ › step through them. Export PDF saves it.

Changing many at once

Tap Select Many and choose the fixtures. The ✓ on a model row takes all of that model. A fixture is ticked only in the row you tapped, not in its other rows.

Each ✓ shows the order you picked it in, from 1. Naming, numbering and addressing follow that order.

ActionWhat it does
Select All / Select NoneTakes or clears everything, folded rows included
NameNumbers the end of the name in the order you selected
NumberSets fixture numbers in the order you selected
AddressRe-addresses them from a universe, start address and gap
BatteryMarks or unmarks them for BATTERY SAVE
New groupBuilds a group from the selection
DeleteRemoves them. Check the count before you confirm

Deleting a fixture also removes its intensity, color and limits, and takes it out of every Scene. HISTORY can undo it.

Deleting from within a group only removes it from that group; the fixture itself stays. If that leaves the group empty, the group is deleted too. The confirmation says so.

Re-patch — moving into free space

  1. Open Patch → Re-patch.
  2. In the address-ordered list, choose the fixture to move.
  3. Tap a free range. The fixture moves to the start of that range.

Only ranges large enough are offered. Where two fixtures overlap, both are shown in red.

Close Gaps, at the top right of Re-patch, packs the fixtures of one universe from address 1, in address order. Gaps you left on purpose are closed up too.

  • It lists only the fixtures that move, with Before and After. Nothing changes until you tap Apply.
  • The fixtures' own DMX addresses do not change. Set each fixture to its After value.
  • A locked fixture's held values stay at its old addresses (chapter 06).
  • The whole pack is one step in HISTORY.

Building groups

  1. Tap ＋ Group and give it a name.
  2. Choose the fixtures in the order you want them on Home.
  3. Tap CREATE.

A new group's name starts with a number, given for you. It is one more than the last numbered group in the group order (1 if there is none).

  • Type FRONT after 2 BACK and you get 3 FRONT.
  • A name you start with a number keeps that number.

Command entry calls a group by this number, as in GROUP 3 (chapter 08).

A fixture can be in several groups. It is not copied: changing it from any group changes the same fixture. Adding it to a group leaves it in All.

Tapping a group name lets you set the name, see the count and address range and layout, or delete it. Edit Group adds fixtures to the group, and holds Fader Order for it under the list of fixtures (chapter 04); Add to an Existing Group puts the current selection into a group you already have.

Group Order, in the row under ＋ Group, sets the order of the groups. It appears once there are two or more groups, and is not shown to a guest.

Drag the handle at the right of a row; Home's model and group buttons and this list then follow the same order. All is not in the list and always comes first. Each move is one step in HISTORY.

RENUMBER in Group Order asks Renumber Groups? first. Renumber All then numbers every group 1, 2, 3 and so on in the order of the list.

The number goes in front of the name and replaces any old one. The order does not change. It is one step in HISTORY.

Whether Patch shows an All row is set in Settings → Settings → Display → Groups → Show the All Row.

Fixtures not in the library (Advanced)

Custom Fixtures holds definitions you add yourself. It is on the Patch tab, under ＋ Fixtures and the list of models. The definitions are available to every show. Deleting a definition does not affect fixtures already patched from it.

From GDTF Share

  1. Open ＋ Browse GDTF Share and SIGN IN with your GDTF Share account.
  2. REFRESH the list, then choose manufacturer, fixture, revision and mode. Search covers every manufacturer.
  3. Read the import report and choose SAVE, SAVE & EDIT or SAVE & PATCH.

SAVE & PATCH opens the patch screen with that definition selected. Remember on This Device stores your sign-in; FORGET removes it. Definitions you already fetched stay. Your sign-in goes to GDTF Share.

From a GDTF file

Tap ＋ Import a GDTF File, tap it again in the panel that opens, pick the .gdtf, check the mode and the import report, then save. No network is needed.

The report lists what could not be carried over. A 16-bit value split across distant addresses keeps only its coarse byte, unused addresses are held as empty slots, and channels on another DMX break are dropped. Where addresses overlap, the earlier channel wins. Unknown functions keep their original names.

A definition marked Imported data is not verified. should be checked against the real fixture. Fix wrong roles with SAVE & EDIT; the fix applies to fixtures you patch from it afterwards. This mode has no channels. means you should pick a different mode.

By hand, from a DMX chart

Open ＋ Build by Hand and start from one of these.

  • Build It Yourself: an empty definition.
  • A template: Intensity, CCT, Bi-color, RGB, HSI, x, y, CCT + HSI, Intensity + RGBW, Full Color, Full Color + White, Multi-emitter or Pixel.

Copy an Existing Fixture, on the same screen, starts from a fixture in the library instead (below).

Give each channel a label, and set the role, 8 or 16 bit, default and real-world unit as needed.

  • Channel numbers and the total are worked out for you.
  • Leave a slot unused if you do not know its role, and you can still drive it from Channels.
  • Save is refused while there is an ERROR.

Each channel also has a Pixel: None, or a number.

  • Channels with the same number make one pixel, marked P1, P2 and so on in the table.
  • When several Intensity channels have no Pixel, an amber note says they move together on one fader. Give each its own Pixel to control them separately.
  • The Pixel template asks for two things: Each Pixel, the template one pixel is built from, and Pixels, how many there are. It then repeats the channels that many times.

By copying an existing one

Open ＋ Build by Hand → Copy an Existing Fixture and choose Manufacturer, Fixture and Mode. The copy is named "… (Modified)" and is listed under MODIFIED in the Manufacturer list. Duplicate and Edit lets you change the name, the color temperature range (shown only when there is a CCT channel), channel roles and names, labels and defaults. The channel count, the 16-bit layout, the ranges and the switch structure cannot be changed.

Free and Kanau Pro

Free sends addresses 1–64 of Universe 1. No feature is limited, and there is no limit on how many fixtures you can patch. Kanau Pro sends every universe and address.

The top line of Settings shows where you stand.

  • While you are on Free: it reads Kanau Free.
  • While you have Kanau Pro: it reads Kanau Pro, in amber.

On the right is a status such as Free, Monthly plan or Lifetime purchase. Tap the line to open the Kanau Pro purchase screen.

Kanau Pro comes as MONTHLY or LIFETIME. Both unlock the same things.

  • MONTHLY: US$7.99 a month. The first month is free. When the free period ends, your subscription starts automatically and renews until you cancel in Manage Subscription.
  • LIFETIME: a single payment of US$149.99.

Buying LIFETIME while you pay for MONTHLY does not stop the subscription. Cancel it in Manage Subscription. Restore Purchases brings back both MONTHLY and LIFETIME.

While on Free, fixtures outside addresses 1–64 and fixtures crossing address 64 are not sent. You can still patch them, and these marks show what is not sent.

  • Home: their round icons go dark and show PRO, and the row with ‹／› shows a red 1–64.
  • The Patch screen: their number and address are crossed out with a red double line, next to PRO.
  • DMX Monitor: the heading of every universe other than Universe 1 shows a red × and PRO.

A guest showing the host's patch does not show these marks.

  • Setting intensity → chapter 04
  • Per-fixture settings → chapter 06
