↑ Contents

04 Setting intensity — Home

The faders on Home. This is the heart of Kanau.

Moving a fader

A fader responds to the distance your finger travels, not to the place you touched. You can drive it from the number, the round icon, or the empty space below the fader. It is built so you can work while looking at the stage instead of at your hand.

The knob grows a little as you touch it, and nothing moves until you have dragged a short way, so resting a finger on it is safe. The light along the fader goes out when the number above it reads 0, so a fader at 0 never looks like it is at 1. If you have set limits, the fader moves within them.

A light haptic tap comes the moment the fader you are moving reaches its upper or lower limit, including a limit you set; it is not repeated while you stay there. ZEN and the grand master do the same. A locked fixture, or a guest that cannot write, gets none.

While you drag, the number, the name shown under the faders and the value appear large at the top of the screen. On a fixture that carries color, the readout also shows the following.

  • That color, as a band
  • The color temperature in kelvin
  • G or M with a number, when the green / magenta tint is off neutral
  • The name of the gel you picked from a table

The gel's name is shown for as long as the color is still the one you set. A color that only happens to match a gel is not named. A white is named from its kelvin value.

A plain dimmer shows none of that. The GRAND, FREE and group master faders show no large readout at all. Read their value from the number above each fader.

FINE

ActionWhat happens
Short tapCycles normal → FINE (1/10) → FINE+ (1/20) → normal
HoldThe next step while held. Back to normal when you let go

Switching mid-drag does not make the value jump. FINE also applies to raw channels and to Pan and Tilt.

Moving several at once

Select two or more round icons, then drag one of the faders. They all move by the same amount, keeping the differences between them. When one reaches a limit the others carry on. Locked fixtures are left out.

In the COLOR panel, the Intensity slider and ± also move each fixture from its own value, and the ratio row scales each fixture from its own level. Only the 0–100 number buttons and typing a value put every fixture on the same value (chapter 05).

The number buttons as a piano

The ＋ − button at the bottom right sets the mode.

ModeWhile a number button is held
LOCK (the default)Nothing changes
＋Goes to the Piano ＋ level, 100 by default. Never above the fixture's upper limit, and never lowers a fixture that is already higher
−Goes to the Piano − level, 0 by default. Never below the fixture's lower limit, and never raises a fixture that is already lower

Let go and it returns to where it was. You can hold several at once, or slide sideways to play them in turn. Locked fixtures do not respond.

The buttons turn red while ＋ or − is armed. It is always LOCK at launch. The two levels are set in Settings → Settings → PIANO → Piano ＋ and Piano −, for this device; when either differs from 100 or 0, the ＋ − button shows it, as ＋80 or −20.

⏻ — output only

Tapping ⏻ turns a fixture's output off and on while keeping the value. It turns purple while off, and the number stays. Moving the fader while it is off does not light anything.

A tap fades over Power Fade. Power Fade is SNAP, 0.5, 1, 1.5 or 2 seconds, 1.5 by default. Set it in Settings → Settings → Fade Times.

ON/OFF is the default. In the fixture's Power Switch you can change it to FLASH ON or FLASH OFF, which last only while held, or to NONE. Locked fixtures do not respond.

Power Switch also has LOCK. With Power Switch set to LOCK, the button in the place of ⏻ turns that fixture's lock on and off. It is the one button a lock does not stop — if it did, a locked fixture could never be unlocked from here.

A fader as a switch

Turn on Switch in a fixture's panel (chapter 06) and its fader becomes a rocker the full length of the fader. ON is at the top and OFF at the bottom. Each tap switches it the moment you press.

  • Value: ON goes to the upper limit and OFF to the lower limit.
  • Display: the number above reads ON or OFF. When it is OFF, the lower face is a bright plate with OFF in bold and the upper face is flat.
  • What does not work: dragging and FINE (ZEN shows a rocker switch instead).

If B.O. or BATTERY SAVE is holding its output down, it looks OFF too. The number above reads OFF, the lower face is the plate with an edge of purple for B.O. or green for BATTERY SAVE, and the upper face is flat. When the hold ends it shows ON again, because its own ON or OFF was never changed.

A fader set as a switch works with the other functions as follows.

  • GM and intensity effects: they do not lower it.
  • BATTERY SAVE: if the fixture is marked for BATTERY SAVE, it turns OFF while BATTERY SAVE is on. It changes at once, with no fade. Its own ON or OFF is left as it was, so it returns when BATTERY SAVE is turned off or when you tap RELEASE for that fixture.
  • B.O.: turns it off.
  • ⏻ and Lock: work as usual.
  • A value that arrives another way, from a Scene, MIDI or the COLOR panel: lands on ON at 50 or above and on OFF below 50. In a Scene fade it switches at the start.
  • The piano: while held, ＋ is ON and − is OFF.

GM and B.O.

Tapping GM at the top opens the masters panel. GRAND, the grand master, is at the right end, with FREE and the group masters to its left (see the next section). Close it with the × at the top left.

  • The GRAND fader sets overall brightness. It is relative, and FINE works on it.
  • B.O., under GRAND, turns the blackout on and off. The GM value is kept.
  • BACK TO 100 is under every master. While that master is down the button is amber, and tapping it puts the master back to 100; at 100 the button is dimmed and cannot be pressed.

Holding GM opens a panel with 100, 75, 50, 25, 12.5 and B.O. B.O. there turns the blackout on; it does not set GM to zero. On iPad the panel has these down the left, the fader in the middle and the fade buttons down the right. On iPhone they are across the top, the fade buttons at the bottom, and the fader takes the room between.

The fade for these buttons is Grand Master Fade: SNAP, 0.5, 1, 1.5 or 2 seconds, in the panel you get by holding GM and in Settings → Settings → Fade Times. Both set the same value. SNAP is the default.

The fade starts gently, is fastest in the middle and lands gently; the time is the whole fade. A guest in a session does not see this setting. Dragging the fader with a finger is always immediate.

WARNING

A fixture with Lock on does not respond to GM or B.O. It stays lit. The count of what is still lit during a blackout, locked fixtures included, is shown next to the green 🔒 at the top of the screen.

Group masters and the FREE master

In the panel you open by tapping GM, FREE sits to the left of GRAND, and the group masters to the left of FREE, in the order of your groups. The name tags are red for GRAND, amber for FREE and white for a group (GROUP and its name). When the group masters do not all fit, ‹ › under the leftmost one turns the page.

A group master scales the intensity of the fixtures in that group in proportion. A fixture in two groups follows the lower of the two masters.

The FREE fader scales the FREE fixtures (chapter 08). It is there even when no fixture is FREE.

On iPhone, the panel you open by holding GM also carries the group masters to the right of the GM fader. The FREE fader in that panel is there when any fixture is FREE or while the FREE master is down. When those do not all fit, ‹ n/m › at the side turns the page.

  • They feel the same as the faders on Home and move at once, with no fade. Letting go is one step in HISTORY.
  • Scenes do not store them, and recalling a Scene does not move them.
  • Locked fixtures and faders set as a switch are not affected.

While a master is down, the following is shown.

  • A group master: that group's button on Home shows its level, such as ↓60, and an unselected button's edge slowly pulses.
  • The FREE master: the page row shows it, such as FREE ↓0.
  • GM: in either case the GM at the top of the screen gets an amber edge that pulses. While GM itself is down, it pulses red as usual.

Choosing what is on the page

Fixtures shows by model and mode; Groups shows All and the groups you built. Tap a name to switch. One fader is always one fixture, even inside a group.

The order under All starts grouped by model, then in patch order, and a group starts in the order you built it. You can change any of them (see Changing the order of the faders below).

‹ and › change page. On the last page, › goes to the first page of the next model; on the first page, ‹ goes to the last page of the previous model. Under Groups, they stay inside the group and never go on to the next one. They stop at the very ends, and never go into or out of All.

Swiping across the band with ‹ and › does the same. Switching between 10 and 5 keeps the fixture you are working on in view.

While you hold a fader, none of these — the names, ‹ and ›, 10 and 5, PIXELS or PIANO — changes what is on the page. Play's BACK and NEXT do not move the Scene either. Pressing one gives a warning vibration instead.

Changing the order of the faders

The faders on Home go in an order you can change. Each page keeps its own: All, every group and every model. Only the order of the columns changes. The light, the limits, the locks, and the fixture number stay with the fixture.

There are two ways in. The first is Fader Order in Patch. Fader Order is in these places.

  • All and models: open the All row or a model under Patched and it is inside.
  • Groups: it is inside Edit Group, under the list of fixtures. It can be pressed once the group has two or more. There the new order is kept with SAVE and thrown away with Cancel.

Fader Order is not shown to a guest, and Patch is closed while BLIND is on.

Fader Order opens a list of the faders in order, starting from the page you pressed it in. ‹ is at the top left. A menu at the top chooses All, a group or a model. Reset Order beside it rebuilds the page the list is showing, from the same bases as RESET ORDER below.

Each row shows the following, from the left.

  • The fader's place
  • The fixture's number, in thin type
  • Its name as it is in Patch (the model's name when none is set), on its Label Color when it has one
  • A handle, at the right

Hold the handle and drag the row up or down: the rows around it move aside, and it goes in where you let go. One row moves at a time.

An amber line under a row marks the end of a page of Home, every 10 or 5 faders. When a fixture on the page has PIXELS open, the list numbers fixtures rather than faders, and no amber lines are shown.

The second way is to make Home itself the editor. Hold the heading above the faders, the one with the page name and ‹ ›. The heading turns into ‹ REORDER, the page name, [n/m] › and DONE. The faders are dimmed and do not respond, so touching them changes no brightness.

Hold a column, from the icon down to the fader, and drag it sideways: the column keeps its look, with a thin green edge, and follows your finger. The columns in between slide over by one place to open the spot where it will go in. It settles there when you let go. The lifted column stays within the columns and never reaches the buttons along the bottom.

While you hold it, its round icon turns green and shows a number: the place it will take if you let go now. The number is counted through all the pages of that button (All, a group or a model), one number per fixture, the same as in the Fader Order list.

A column can cross pages.

  1. Drag the column until its outer edge is over the last column of the page (or the first).
  2. Hold it there for about half a second, and the page turns. While you wait, the › (or ‹) in the heading fills with a green ring.
  3. Let go. The column goes in on the page showing when you let go.

These rules apply when turning the page.

  • If you move back or let go before the ring fills, the page does not turn and the column goes in where it is.
  • Grabbing a column does not start the wait. It starts once the column has moved.
  • Staying there turns no more pages. Take the column off the edge and back to turn the next one.
  • It never turns past the first or last page, and the page-name buttons such as All or a group do not change.

‹ and ›, and the buttons that choose the page, still work, and carry on reordering the page you pressed. A fixture with PIXELS open moves as one block. Reordering will not start while a finger is on a fader, and a warning vibration says so.

In place of the buttons along the bottom there is one key, RESET ORDER. Press it and choose a base: Patch Order, Fixture Number, DMX or Model (a model's page has no Model).

The page being reordered is rebuilt the moment you choose, as one step in HISTORY. Pressing the key alone, or Cancel, changes nothing.

While you reorder, the ⏻ row of each column becomes a lightbulb button. Press it and that fixture draws one peak of brightness, so you can see on stage which fixture the column is. The ⏻ row does not grab the column.

  • A fixture that is on: goes down to 0 in 0.5 s, up to 100 in 0.5 s, holds for 1 s, and returns to its level in 0.5 s.
  • A fixture that is off: goes up to 100 in 0.5 s, holds for 1 s, and goes out in 0.5 s.

Pressing the lightbulb does not change faders, ⏻, Scenes or HISTORY. Locked fixtures, fixtures in a universe whose output is off, and anything during B.O. do not light. GM and BATTERY SAVE still apply. On a guest, the host lights it.

Tap DONE to finish. It also ends when you leave Home, when the app goes to the background, when you become a guest, and when you enter or leave BLIND. GM, BATTERY SAVE and SCREEN LOCK keep working during it.

The order belongs to the show: it is saved in the show file, and a guest sees the same order. One move is one step in HISTORY, shown as order.

The host, a device on its own and a guest allowed to control can change the order. A guest's change is made on the host.

MIDI knobs and Switch N follow positions, so they follow the new order. So do the direction of an effect, the direction of PIXELS and the rows of the Fixture Sheet.

A show with no order of its own opens in Model order. Fixture Number in Reset Order sorts once, when you choose it; typing the fixture numbers again later does not re-sort the faders.

The buttons along the bottom

  • COLOR: needs a selection.
  • EFFECT: always opens. With a selection it opens that selection's effect panel, and with nothing selected the list of running effects (chapter 09).
  • PIXELS: goes gray when it has nothing to open. With a selection, that is when no selected fixture on the page has pixels. With none, it is when no fixture on the page has pixels.

Working pixels on their own

Tapping PIXELS opens the cells of the selected pixel fixtures on the page, or of every pixel fixture on the page when nothing is selected, as their own faders. It never opens or closes a fixture on another page. The cells sit right after the fixture's own fader, with number buttons .1, .2 and so on, and each carries its own intensity and color.

Tap again to fold them. Folding a fixture lets go of its pixel selection.

A fixture with pixels carries P above its value. A fixture whose pixel order is inverted (chapter 06) carries R instead, and its pixel faders run the other way: the leftmost is the last pixel.

A fixture whose address overlaps another carries a red ! above its value (chapter 03).

Selecting a cell opens PIXELS for its fixture. A fixture is selected whole or by cell, never both. A fixture selected whole shows a faint ring on its cells, and tapping one cell lets go of just that cell.

Select more than one cell and they move together on one fader, the same way fixtures do. Each keeps its distance from the others, and the ones that reach an end stop there.

A cell's fader is the percentage of the fixture's own fader (the parent) that the cell gives out. It runs from 0 to 100, and a cell you have not touched is at 100. The light that comes out is parent × cell ÷ 100.

Lowering the parent does not move the cells' numbers or knobs. The fill of a cell's bar reaches the height of the light actually coming out, and the part the parent is holding down is marked with the same amber ↓ as a group master. Raising a cell while the parent is at 0 leaves it dark: the parent never rises by itself. Select the parent and move it, and all its cells change together.

CLEAR n only clears the selection. Values and outputs are untouched.

ZEN — one large fader

Tap ZEN in a fixture's panel for a black screen with one large fader and its value. It is there for fixtures whose intensity you can set. It also opens from ZEN in the Play list (at the end of this section).

It opens on a selection as well: hold a round icon, or open COLOR, or hold a model or group button. The name at the bottom says what you have: 3 fixtures, or KEY · 8 fixtures.

With more than one, the one fader raises and lowers a shape of levels. The shape is each fixture's level with the fader at 100. Take two fixtures at 100 and 50: raised from 0, both brighten in the same proportion, and at the top they stop at 100 and 50. They go no higher.

The number on screen is how much of the shape is up. Opening changes nothing.

The shape is remembered. The number you see when ZEN opens is decided as follows.

  • If the levels are still a share of the remembered shape, the number starts at that share.
  • If every fixture is at 0, the number is 0 and they come up in the remembered shape.
  • If a Home fader or a Scene recall has changed the levels, the levels as they are become the new shape and the number starts at 100.

A ZEN group's shape is saved in the show. What moves is each fixture's own fader, so a Scene records it. Each stops inside its own limits, and locked fixtures do not move. This is a different rule from the Intensity slider in the COLOR panel (chapter 05).

Drag anywhere on the screen to work it, relative as usual. FINE, under TILT at the top left, is the same FINE as on Home. Tap it for FINE, FINE+ and off, or hold it for as long as you need it.

On a single fixture the settings at the top right hold the limits, TILT's angle and FIXTURE SETTINGS. FIXTURE SETTINGS opens the fixture's panel on its SETUP tab and comes back to ZEN when you close it. With more than one, these settings are not there.

A fixture set as Switch shows a rocker instead of a fader: each press turns it ON at its upper limit or OFF at its lower.

The way out is the × at the top left. Tapping the screen does not leave. Neither does moving the fader and letting go.

TILT at the top left hands the fader to the angle of the phone. The 0 AT angle in the settings is the bottom of its travel and the 100 AT angle is the top. The ends are 0 and 100 with no limits set, and the limits themselves where you have set them.

It keeps working after you take your hand away, and it follows a quick hand without lagging behind. It does not grab at once: it waits until the tilt meets the level the fader is already on, so nothing jumps.

Lying flat, the phone is at 0°. 0 AT is 0°, 15°, 30° or 45° and 100 AT is 90°, 60° or 45°, starting at 0° and 90°.

The two stay at least 30° apart, so a pair that is too close cannot be pressed. A small diagram beside them shows the range you chose. The closer the two angles, the less movement it takes to reach the top.

0 AT and 100 AT can also be set under ZEN TILT in Settings → Settings. It is the same setting, so a change in either place shows in both. With several fixtures selected, set it under ZEN TILT in Settings → Settings.

Lowering the phone's top edge below flat keeps the fader at the bottom until the phone points straight down. Continuing toward face down brings the fader up as far as you turn, reaching the top when the phone lies face down. The value does not jump in any position.

Reaching the top gives a short vibration, and the phone keeps vibrating while the fader stays there. Reaching the bottom gives one short vibration. Pulling the fader with a finger turns TILT off, and so does leaving ZEN.

+ FADER at the top right adds another fader: up to three on iPhone and five on iPad, counting the first. It opens a list of Groups and Fixtures; tap one to add it as a fader of its own and close the list. A fixture already on another fader is dimmed.

The screen divides into columns, each worked on its own, relative as usual, with its number at the top and its name at the bottom. A group reads like KEY · 8 fixtures and follows the rule above. Each column has its own ⚙ at the bottom, with its limits, FIXTURE SETTINGS and, from the second column on, Remove fader.

With two or more faders the ⚙ at the top right is gone, and TILT switches off and is not shown; FINE takes its place. When you are back to one fader, both return, with TILT off.

ZEN in the Play list opens a panel for choosing what ZEN works on. From the top, the panel has the following.

  • SELECTED: what you have selected on Home. Tap it to go straight into ZEN. SAVE beside it keeps that selection as a ZEN group.
  • Fixtures: tap a fixture to open ZEN on it. The button to the right of the heading, such as All · 24, narrows the list to one model or one Home group. Closing the panel puts it back to All.
  • Groups: lists the ZEN groups and the groups from Home. Tap a group to open ZEN on it.

New Group makes an empty ZEN group. Edit on a ZEN group's row sets its name, the fixtures for the first fader (①), and the faders for the second and third (② and ③) (added with + FADER), and Delete Group removes it. ② and ③ are kept, and appear as columns when you open ZEN on that group.

Next

05 Setting color — COLOR

Color and intensity for one fixture or many.

NOTE

What you see depends on what the fixture actually has. A one-channel dimmer shows only Intensity. Kanau does not show controls a fixture does not have.

Opening the panel

HowWhat it works on
Hold a fixture iconThat one fixture
Hold a cell iconThat cell
Select round icons, then COLOR, or hold one of the selected iconsEverything selected. A fixture with PIXELS closed counts whole; with PIXELS open, its pixels count — all of them when its own icon is selected, or only the pixel icons you selected
Hold a model or group buttonEvery fixture in it. All means every fixture

Tabs run across the top of the panel: LIGHT, MOVE, GRADIENT and SETUP.

  • LIGHT: intensity and color.
  • MOVE: the position and beam (chapter 07).
  • GRADIENT: the intensity and color you lay across fixtures (below).
  • SETUP: the names, Fade Time and the fixture settings (chapter 06).

MOVE and GRADIENT appear only for a selection that can use them. When the panel is laid out in two columns on iPad there is no SETUP tab; the names and the fixture settings are in the right column.

In a panel opened by holding a round icon, these are available.

  • ZEN (LIGHT): opens one large fader (chapter 04).
  • EFFECT (LIGHT): opens that fixture's effects (chapter 09).
  • The NEXT row (SETUP): sits under the Fade Time heading and shows the Delay and Fade into the next Scene (chapter 08).

On iPhone, SETUP is not a tab that swaps the contents but a shortcut to the Settings that continue below. Scroll past the end of LIGHT, MOVE or GRADIENT and the Settings heading follows, with the names, Fade Time and the fixture settings.

  • Tapping SETUP: takes you to the Settings heading.
  • Tapping LIGHT, MOVE or GRADIENT: takes you back to the top of its contents.
  • Opening from ZEN's ⚙: the panel opens at Settings.
  • Which tab is lit: while the Settings heading is above the middle of the screen, SETUP is lit and LIGHT, MOVE and GRADIENT are not.

‹ and › appear in the following panels. They do not appear on a cell's panel or on a panel for several fixtures.

  • The panel opened from a fixture in the Patch tab
  • The panel opened by holding one fixture's round icon on Home

They move to the previous or next fixture of the current Home scope (All, a model or a group), across pages, and stop at the ends. The open tab is kept. A Label, Name or number you have typed is committed before the move.

A panel for a selection names what it works on under its title, such as 3 pixels or 2 fixtures. Color, Intensity and the limits then act on those alone, and pixels you did not select stay as they are.

Any selection opens COLOR, even fixtures with no color.

  • Only fixtures with no color: the panel has Intensity, the limits, Lock and the other settings but no color.
  • A mix: only the fixtures that have color take it.

On iPhone a line at the bottom of the panel names the Scene you are working in.

  • AUTO UPDATE: a red A with RECORDING
  • MANUAL UPDATE: an amber M with UPDATE
  • A locked Scene: LOCKED in green

UPDATE there records the current state into that Scene, as UPDATE in Scenes does. It can be pressed when it blinks.

Intensity and color

ItemHow it works
Intensity0 to 100, by slider, typing, ± buttons, presets or the ratio keys
Color Temperature (CCT)In kelvin, within the fixture's range
Green / MagentaThe green–magenta correction. The 0 button returns it to neutral
CrossfadeThe balance between the white side and the color side. Which way round is up to the fixture
RGB and emittersR, G, B, W, Amber, Lime, Cyan and whatever else the fixture carries
Hue / Saturation / CIE x / CIE yShown on fixtures that have them

Intensity ±5 and ±10 snap to multiples of 5 or 10: from 47, +10 gives 50. With several fixtures selected, each one moves from its own level.

  • A fixture at 100 stays at 100 on +.
  • A fixture at 0 stays at 0 on −.
  • A locked fixture does not move.

The presets are 0, 10, 20, 30, 50, 75 and 100. When the selected fixtures are at different levels, the number reads — in amber and no preset lights. The slider stays at the first fixture's level. The number comes back once they match.

Below a dividing line, 1/8, 1/4 and 1/2 set the level to that part of what it is now, and ×2, ×4 and ×8 multiply it, up to 100.

With two or more fixtures or pixels that have intensity, the Intensity section of the GRADIENT tab (below) has one field. It starts empty and shows the levels as you press the keys, such as 0 THRU 100 THRU 0. That same row is written under it as an example.

To type the levels:

  1. Tap the field and a keypad opens below. Its keys are 7 8 9 THRU, 4 5 6 DEL, 1 2 3 C, 0 ENTER; the phone's keyboard is not used.
  2. Type levels with THRU between them.
  3. Press ENTER, which sets the fixtures and closes the keypad.

Tap the field again to close it without changing anything. The first key you press after opening decides what happens.

  • A digit: a new row of levels starts.
  • THRU or DEL: carries on from the old row.
  • ENTER: sets the row again.

How the levels are spread depends on how many you type.

  • One level: sets every fixture to it.
  • Two levels: the fixtures go in even steps from the first to the second, in fader order.
  • Three or more levels: each level sits on the nearest fixture and the ones between follow a straight line. 0 THRU 100 THRU 0 goes up and back, so the middle lands on 100: with five fixtures, 0, 50, 100, 50, 0.
  • A level that falls exactly between two fixtures: gives both the same value. With ten fixtures, 0 THRU 100 THRU 0 THRU 50 THRU 10 gives 0, 50, 100, 50, 0, 0, 25, 50, 30, 10.

A locked fixture does not move, and each fixture stays inside its own limits. It works with mixed models. Each ENTER is one step in HISTORY.

The CCT presets are 2700, 3000, 3200, 4300, 5000, 5600, 6500 and 10000 K. Beyond the fixture's range you land on its limit, marked MIN or MAX. A fixture with only two color temperatures shows two buttons instead of a slider.

Where a fixture has more than one crossfade, the later ones appear just above the controls they feed.

Gels

ItemWhat it is
Gel presetsLEE and Rosco presets for fixtures with RGB. Separate tables for 3200 K and 5600 K
Preset / GelThe fixture's own built-in gels or color presets, chosen by number
Gels → x/yThe makers' own CIE x/y tables, for fixtures with x and y: LEE, 295 filters, and Rosco, 1,079. Choose the light source from the menu at the top (see below the table)

Notes on the table:

  • The Gels → x/y key: once you pick one, the key reads that gel, such as LEE 002 Rose Pink, until x or y is changed another way.
  • The Gels → x/y list: rows sit under the maker's own headings, and Rosco's discontinued filters carry its mark. Roscolene is not included.

The RGB values under Gel presets come from Astera's published color data. They carry no brightness, so set that with the fader. With a fixture's built-in presets, the app cannot always show which one is selected.

The x/y tables are the makers' values, sent as they are. Rosco's are its myColor figures, which use the 10° observer.

On a fixture whose Crossfade runs from a color temperature to a color, picking a color moves a Crossfade that sits at the color-temperature end over to the color end, so the color shows. This holds for the picker, a gel preset and Gels → x/y alike.

The list stays open after you pick, so you can try one after another. A long list has an index down its right edge — the hundreds of the gel number, or the first letter of each heading — and tapping one jumps there. Close it with × at the top left.

Whether it appears at all is set in Settings → Settings → Display → Gels → Gel presets.

Saving colors you use often

  • Save this color stores a color under ★. A saved color is kept per model and mode, and holds the Crossfade and, where the fixture has them, the color temperature and G/M. A ★ that holds neither leaves them as they are.
  • Save this temperature stores a color temperature. That one is shared across models.

Saved colors and color temperatures appear as buttons under the Favorites heading.

Saving opens the new button's editor so you can name it. Its Save cannot be pressed while the name is empty: Name this color asks for one. Closing the editor without a name throws the new color away.

Tap a stored button to apply it. Hold to rename, edit or delete. Edit covers everything it stores: RGB or the emitters, x/y, the Crossfade, and the color temperature and G/M.

Advanced Color

Advanced Color gathers the controls the app works out for itself, rather than the fixture's own channels.

In the picker, hue runs across and saturation down. Brightness is the fader's job.

  • Tap: tap anywhere to place the color.
  • Drag: take the round handle. A drag that starts anywhere else scrolls the panel.

RGB, the Hue and Saturation worked out from RGB, and CMY (255 − RGB) appear on fixtures that can take them. On a fixture that takes only Hue and Saturation, or only x and y, they restate the fixture's color at full strength, and setting them reaches the light; brightness stays with the fader. A fixture's own Hue, Saturation or CMY channels are not repeated here.

Several fixtures, and several models

In this panel, whatever you touch lands on the same value for everything selected. That is true of the color sliders, the Intensity presets from 0 to 100, typing and the stored colors alike.

There are these exceptions.

  • Moving Intensity: its slider, its ± buttons and the ratio row under it (1/8 to ×8) move each fixture from its own level, so they do not all land on one value.
  • The GRADIENT tab: its color layout and its THRU row give each fixture something different on purpose.

With two or more fixtures selected, or two or more pixels with PIXELS open, a GRADIENT tab appears. The tabs read LIGHT | MOVE | GRADIENT | SETUP, or LIGHT | GRADIENT | SETUP when none of them has a MOVE panel.

GRADIENT is not there in the following cases. A panel last left on GRADIENT opens on LIGHT in those cases.

  • One closed fixture
  • A single pixel
  • The panel opened from Patch

GRADIENT holds these.

  • The Intensity section: comes first and holds the keypad field.
  • The Color section: comes below it. It has the layout buttons described under Coloring along the pixels below, and a color band for whatever the layout is setting.

The Color section appears only for fixtures of one model in one mode with PIXELS closed. With anything else, GRADIENT holds only Intensity. With PIXELS closed, the LIGHT tab has no layout buttons and no keypad row: it writes the same color to everything selected.

With different models selected, only Intensity, CCT, G/M and ★ appear. Open one model on its own to set RGB and emitters. CCT is held within each fixture's own range.

Pixels and repeated color groups

Hold a cell icon to set that cell's color and intensity. Changing the fixture's own color sets every cell except those you changed by hand, which keep their own. The fixture's own Intensity applies across all the cells. Intensity on a cell's own panel moves that cell only.

Where a mode carries the same color role more than once, such as Gel 1 and Gel 2, the later groups appear lower in the panel. Every color group is stored in a Scene, and comes back with it as long as the fixture is still in the same mode.

Coloring along the pixels — PIXELS

With PIXELS open on Home, the LIGHT tab of a pixel fixture's COLOR panel starts with a PIXELS section. It lays color out along the pixels in one go, on every fixture you have selected. It appears only where the pixels have color channels, such as RGB or Hue and Saturation.

Select only some pixels and it works on just those. They are treated as one line in their order on Home, and EACH and ACROSS do not appear.

ButtonWhat it lays out
SOLIDEvery pixel follows the fixture's own color
GRADIENTSTART on the first pixel, END on the last, blended in between
ALTERNATECOLOR 1 and COLOR 2 taking turns, or three colors with COLOR 3
RAINBOWThe hue circle along the pixels

The button you pressed lights amber, and so does the end or color you are setting — START, END, or COLOR 1 to COLOR 3. The sliders, presets and gels below then write to that one. There is nothing to confirm: the light changes as you go, and HISTORY steps back.

  • GRADIENT: START and END hold an intensity as well as a color, and the pixels between them change intensity little by little too. Spread narrows or widens the blend. The blend runs through color temperature too, so START can be a warm white and END a color, on pixels that have those channels.
  • ALTERNATE: Colors sets two or three, and Pixels per Color how many pixels each one takes.
  • RAINBOW: Start Hue is the hue of the first pixel, and Span how far round the circle it goes along the fixture — 100% is once round. The 100%, 200%, 300% and 400% buttons under Span set it directly, and 100% puts it back to the default. Only Intensity is left below, because the rainbow decides the color.

These change the pattern. None of them appear on SOLID.

  • REVERSE: swaps the ends, the colors or the direction.
  • MIRROR: makes the pattern symmetrical, with the same color at both ends. It does not work with ALTERNATE.
  • SHIFT − and SHIFT +: move the pattern one pixel. The pixel pushed off one end comes back at the other.

On GRADIENT, they all move intensity along with color (on FIXTURES, with PIXELS closed, color only).

The row of dots is the first selected fixture's pixels, or every fixture's under ACROSS. Each dot is read from what is going out.

Tap a dot to set that pixel alone with the controls below, and tap it again or ALL to go back. Setting START or END again redraws the blend, pixels set by hand included.

With several fixtures, the pattern is laid out in one of these ways.

  • EACH: each fixture takes the same pattern from its own first pixel.
  • ACROSS: joins them into one line in their order on Home, from the first pixel of the first fixture to the last pixel of the last.

The pattern follows the pixel numbers, so a fixture with inverted pixels (chapter 06) starts from the same side on stage. Its own dots show START on the right.

＋ saves the pattern and its colors as a palette and asks for a name. Tap a palette to apply it, and hold it to rename or delete it.

  • Where they are kept: per model, on this device. One made on 16 pixels fits a fixture with 4.
  • What is not saved: the shift and ACROSS.
  • With different models selected: the palette row is not there.

Fixtures with Lock on and fixtures running a color effect are left as they are. A Scene stores the colors like any other.

FIXTURES — one fixture as one step

Select two or more fixtures of the same model in the same mode, with PIXELS closed, and the GRADIENT tab shows the same section under FIXTURES.

  • Order: each fixture is one step, in their order on Home. There is no EACH or ACROSS.
  • SOLID: gives them all the first fixture's color.
  • Pixel colors: setting a fixture's color here clears its own pixel colors, so the fixture's color shows.
  • Palettes: shared with the pixel section of the same model.

While a color effect is running

A color effect — RAINBOW, the colored fires, lightning and fluorescents — runs on any fixture that can make color, whatever mode it is in: RGB, CMY, Hue and Saturation, or xy.

While one runs, the color controls for that fixture are there to read, not to touch. A band at the top of the panel carries a dot lit in the color going out and the name of the effect, and says the color cannot be edited. Intensity still works.

The values under the band are the color that comes back when the effect stops, so they stay where you left them.

A mode with no color, or an effect that does not move color, leaves the color controls working as usual.

The band also carries the values going out at this moment. Hold the round fixture icon to open this panel and read them.

06 Per-fixture settings

Limits, Lock and the raw channels of a single fixture.

In the panel you get from holding a fixture icon, from COLOR, or from holding a model or group button, tap the SETUP tab at the top. On iPad, when the panel is in two columns, the settings are in the right column; on iPhone they are under Settings, further down the panel.

Limits, Lock, FREE, Power Switch, BATTERY SAVE and Switch can be set for several fixtures at once. Mixed values show in amber, as — or n of m (for Switch, n of m set as Switch), and changing one applies it to all of them. Channels, Mode, Channel Roles and Patch appear only with a single fixture open.

The panel opened from a fixture in the Patch tab has BATTERY SAVE, Switch, the Invert rows, the limits and Label Color below the Re-patch button. It has no Lock, Power Switch or Channels; those are in the panel from holding the fixture's icon.

On a panel for selected pixels, the settings reach as follows.

  • The limits: change only those pixels.
  • Switch: is not there.
  • Lock, Power Switch, BATTERY SAVE and Label Color: act on the whole fixture.

Name and display

The title at the top of the panel is read-only: the fixture number and the name shown under the faders. At the top of SETUP, two lines name the fixture.

  • Label: the display name every fixture of the same model in the same mode shares. Change it and they all change, while a fixture in another mode keeps its own Label. It starts as the name from Patch. Clear the field and the model's own name shows faintly in it, and when you commit the empty field the model's name comes back.
  • Name: belongs to this fixture alone. Leave it empty and the Label is shown.

Under the faders, in titles and in the large readout, a fixture shows its Name if it has one, and its Label if not.

In the panel opened from the Patch tab, or by holding a fixture's round icon on Home, ‹ and › move to the previous or next fixture. They do not appear on a cell's panel or on a panel for several fixtures. In the panel from the Patch tab, Re-patch turns the title into a field for the fixture's name in Patch, the name the patch lists show.

Label Color is the background of the number. No label color clears it.

Limits

Lower Limit and Upper Limit set the range you can work in. Change them with ±1 and ±5, or clear them. Outside a limit, Home shows orange hatching.

A cell's limits apply inside the fixture's own. If the fixture is capped at 50, a cell capped at 80 still cannot pass 50.

Lock

WARNING

Fixture Lock holds a fixture's output where it is (an effect running when you lock keeps running). The grand master, blackout, BATTERY SAVE, MIDI, the session and Scene recalls do not change it — a locked fixture will not go out when you press blackout. Check your locks before a take.

With Lock on, the fixture's output is held. Faders, piano mode, ⏻, color, raw channels, GM, B.O., BATTERY SAVE, MIDI and the session all leave it alone, and so do Scene recalls.

Lock holds the DMX values at the fixture's addresses just before they go out. Unlocking returns the output to what Kanau is working out now, with the grand master, B.O., BATTERY SAVE and the rest applied.

Lock also behaves as follows.

  • A locked fixture's address or mode changes, or it is deleted: the old addresses keep sending the held values, and a red note in the Patch section says so.
  • A lock left without its fixture: appears in DMX Monitor, where UNLOCK releases it.
  • Saving: locks are saved in the show.
  • An effect that was running: an effect running when you lock keeps running. It stays at the intensity the fixture had when you locked, so lowering the grand master afterwards does not dim it.
  • Effects on a locked fixture: an effect cannot be applied, changed or stopped on a locked fixture.

Locks and limits belong to the console, not to a Scene. No Scene records them, and a recall never locks, unlocks or moves a locked fixture.

Unlocking does not bring in a Scene's values on the spot: the faders and other values stay as they were when you locked. The Scene's values arrive with the next recall.

Lock This Scene is a different thing (chapter 08), and chapter 08 covers what a Scene stores.

With several fixtures selected and some of them locked, tapping Lock clears every lock. With none locked, tapping Lock locks them all.

Locking during a piano, FLASH or HIT press puts the temporary value back first, then holds. Changing limits while locked does not move the current value; it is brought into the new range when you unlock.

The other settings

ItemWhat it is
Power SwitchWhat ⏻ does: NONE, ON/OFF, FLASH ON, FLASH OFF or LOCK. ON/OFF is the default. LOCK makes each press lock or unlock the fixture
BATTERY SAVEMarks this fixture for BATTERY SAVE (see below the table)
Invert Pixels / Invert Pan / Invert TiltInvert Pan and Invert Tilt reverse the direction of Move effects on this fixture only. Invert Pixels reverses the order of this fixture's pixels (see below the table)
SwitchTurns this fader into an ON / OFF switch (chapter 04). Not the same as Power Switch, which sets what ⏻ does
FREEScene recalls (the list, NEXT and BACK) leave this fixture where it is; faders and the piano still move it (see below the table)
DMX ModeIn the panel opened from Patch, shows the current DMX mode. On a fixture with more than one mode, Change beside it opens Re-patch at the mode list
Channel RolesCorrects the role and name of each channel. Addresses do not move

Notes on the table:

  • While BATTERY SAVE is on: a green band sits just under the panel's title. It shows BATTERY SAVE 50% and 80 → 40 (the fader level → what goes out).
  • RELEASE: sits at the right of the green band. It brings this fixture back to its fader level until BATTERY SAVE is turned off, and turns into an amber RELEASED.
  • Invert Pixels: the fixture's pixel faders on Home mirror with it.
  • Invert on a locked fixture: all three are dimmed and cannot be switched.
  • FREE: GM, B.O. and BATTERY SAVE still apply. A fixture is FREE or locked, never both (chapter 08).

Use Channel Roles when a patched fixture has channels being treated as the wrong function. To carry the fix into fixtures you patch later, edit the definition under Custom Fixtures instead.

With one fixture open, the bottom of SETUP shows these.

  • Its Patch (universe and address range)
  • DMX Mode
  • DMX Values (what is going out now), folded

Channels — the raw DMX (Advanced)

Use the dedicated controls for color, position and the rest first. Channels is for reaching functions those controls do not cover, one DMX channel at a time.

Channels lists everything in DMX order, under Dimmer, Color, Position, Gobo, Beam, Focus, Shapers and Control. Empty groups are hidden.

Kind of rowHow to work it
A continuous valueSlider, typing, or − and +
Named values and rangesA menu up to 12 entries, a searchable list beyond that
Commands like Reset or Lamp OffHold for the stated time. Let go early to cancel. Commands with no time are a tap
A row marked FADER or COLORDriven by a dedicated control. Where the console has a knob for it, such as CCT or G/M, the row carries a slider and a number field to edit it here; where it has none, such as white or strobe, the row is only a label
A row that depends on another channelShows what is available in the current state. When the row is not in use, a note names the channel and the range that switch it off

On a fixture whose second light source has its own dimmer, such as the Aura ring of a MAC Aura XIP, that dimmer is a row of its own here. The fader scales it: what goes out is the row's value times the fader, so with the fader at 0 it is dark.

Intensity effects do not move it. B.O., GM and BATTERY SAVE act on it as well.

DMX at the top right switches between raw values and percentages. Home on a row returns it to its default; on Pan and Tilt that needs a hold. It is unavailable when nothing has been changed.

Changes to raw channels are recorded in HISTORY. Whether they also go into the current Scene follows chapter 08.

  • AUTO UPDATE: writes them as you work.
  • MANUAL UPDATE: waits for UPDATE.
  • A Scene with Lock This Scene on: records nothing.

On a pixel fixture, the fixture's own panel carries its own channels and a cell panel carries that cell's.

Changing the patch or the mode

Edit from Re-patch in the Patch section. You can see and change the universe and address, fixture number, model and mode.

  • Universe and Address: set them by typing or with − and +. Anything other than a plain number is ignored.
  • Channel Roles and Delete This Fixture: are there too. The settings below Re-patch are hidden while Re-patch is open.
  • Next Free: moves the fixture to the next gap.

Each change here is one step in HISTORY.

Change Mode shows the range before and after and any fixtures it would overlap, before you confirm.

  • Apply to all: changes every fixture of the same model that is in the same mode as this one. Fixtures in another mode are left as they are.
  • Fixtures after it: do not move on their own.
  • Change & Move to Next Free: also appears when the new mode would overlap or run past channel 512. Move to shows where the fixture goes.

Kanau changes only its own patch: set each fixture's own DMX address to its Move to value.

After a confirmation, Delete This Fixture removes the fixture from the whole patch, not only from a group, along with its values and settings, and takes it out of every Scene. HISTORY can undo it.

TEST — check the fixtures

A mode for checking by eye, on the morning of a rig or before kit goes out, that gobos do not stick and that the colors, pixels and head movement work. The steps are built for each model from its fixture data. The test does not change the show.

There are two ways in.

  • From a fixture's panel: at the very bottom of SETUP in a fixture's panel, there is TEST MODE, with the same amber heading as Advanced. Tap it to open it. It tests that panel's fixtures.
  • From Settings: open Settings → Settings → TEST MODE. Choose the fixtures with the row at the top (Fixtures | Groups, with ALL and a button for each group) and the list of fixtures: tap a row to select or deselect it, or hold a button to select all of its fixtures. It opens with the fixtures selected on Home.

Both offer the same choices.

  1. Point the heads somewhere you can see and bring the light up. The test moves around where they point now.
  2. Choose the kind (SIMPLE / FULL), Items (what to run; only what those models have is listed) and the speed (SLOW / NORMAL / FAST). With two or more fixtures you also choose how to show it: TOGETHER, all at once, or ONE BY ONE. The number of fixtures and the time it takes read like 24 FIXTURES · 4:32.
  3. START TEST asks first, noting that moving heads swing to the ends of their pan and tilt. Press START TEST again to begin.
KindWhat it runs
SIMPLEColor temperature, Green / Magenta, color (RGB or other mixing; the color wheel if there is no mixing) and pixels
FULLWhatever the model has of the items listed below the table

Notes on the table:

  • What FULL runs: the full range of pan and tilt, dimmer, color mixing, color temperature, Green / Magenta, pixels, color wheel, gobos, animation gobos and rotation. It also runs prism, iris, frost, blades, zoom, focus, built-in effects (MACRO) and strobe.

Everything outside the step being tested is set to open white: the shutter open, wheels on open or white, built-in effects on no effect. Values that are commands, such as a reset, are never sent. Control channels such as the lamp and the fans are not touched.

What each step does:

  • DIMMER (FULL): up from 0 to 100% over 10 seconds, then back to 0 over 10 seconds.
  • CCT: stops for 2 seconds each at the lowest, 3200 K, 5600 K and the highest. Only on models with a color temperature table; points outside the range are skipped.
  • G/M: pauses briefly at each end before coming back.
  • PIXELS: lights the pixels one at a time from pixel 1.
  • STROBE: runs once for each kind of strobe the fixture has. The kinds are Strobe, Pulse, Random and so on, named as in the data. It rises from the slow end to the fast end over 6 seconds and holds the fast end for 2 seconds. Rotation (ROTATION) works the same way.
  • MACRO (FULL): lights one built-in effect for 3 seconds, then stops and waits. › goes on to the next.
  • BLINK: runs only when chosen in Items. It flashes at 1, 2, 5.5, 11 and 22 Hz for 2 seconds each. 22 Hz shows WIRE LIMIT: Kanau sends 44 times a second, so it cannot send a faster flash.

When the fixtures include ones with lamps, STRIKE LAMP shows at the very top of the test screen. Press it to send the lamp-on command to one fixture at a time, for the number of seconds in the data (5 seconds if there is none). Check by eye whether the lamps came on. There is no key to turn the lamps off.

During the test, everything below the status line becomes the test screen. The status line, with GM and the rest, stays in view.

  • At the top, TEST MODE, which step it is (such as 3 / 7) and the time left. When GM is not at 100% or B.O. is on, GM 80% or B.O. shows beside it. The numbers on the screen are the values being sent, after GM and B.O.
  • The current step's name (such as PIXELS or GOBO) in large type, and under it what is happening now (RED, PIXEL 5 / 16, SLOT 3 / 8 and so on).
  • The values moving now on one line (such as ≈ 3190 K · DMX 45). Under it, every channel being tested, with its name, its DMX value, the name of its range and its value in K, Hz, degrees or %. Values partway through a range are marked ≈.
  • A progress bar and the fixtures being tested (under ONE BY ONE, the current fixture is shown large).
  • All the steps in order, with ✓ on the ones done and ▶ on the current one. When different models are tested together, each model's current state is shown too.
  • The large ‹ / › go back or forward one item within the step, and « BACK STEP / NEXT STEP » below them go back or forward a whole step. PAUSE (which becomes RESUME) and EXIT are there too.

When it ends it stops on open white and shows DONE. EXIT brings back the light from before the test.

  • GM and B.O. still work during the test. Locked fixtures do not move.
  • It is not available on a guest or during BLIND.
Next
  • Position and beam → chapter 07
  • Which lock does what → chapter 10

07 Position and beam

Pan, tilt, zoom, iris, frost and gobo on moving lights.

Opening MOVE

Hold a fixture's round icon to open its panel, then switch to MOVE at the top. The MOVE tab is there whenever the selection holds a fixture with head or optics rows. The tab you left open is the one that opens next time.

A fixture with only strobe or effect channels has no MOVE. Its rows are under Channels (chapter 06), on the LIGHT tab.

At the top of MOVE is a button for each section the selected fixtures have. Each is one of POSITION, GOBO, BEAM, FOCUS and SHAPERS. Tap one and only that section is shown below.

The section you last opened is remembered, and MOVE opens on it next time. When there is only one section, these buttons are not shown.

Under these buttons is the Focus row. It stays in the same place whichever section is open, so you can sharpen the beam while you set a gobo or the shutters.

  • When no selected fixture has focus: the row is not shown.
  • A focus chosen by name, such as Auto Focus: it is inside the FOCUS section.

MOVE works on everything you have selected. Where the whole selection shares a value, the row shows it, and where they differ it reads —.

% and DMX at the right of the first row of the open section switch between the fixture's own units and the raw DMX number. It is the same switch as the one under Channels and in DMX Monitor, so the whole console follows it. On DMX a field reads 0–255, or 0–65535 where the row is 16-bit.

Fine adjustment with FINE

Tap FINE at the right of the Focus row to move values in small amounts.

  • Switching: each short tap goes FINE (1/10) → FINE+ (1/20) → off. Hold it and it works only while held.
  • Slider: while FINE is on, a touch does not jump the value. It moves by 1/10 of your finger (1/20 on FINE+).
  • Step keys: they become 1/10 as wide. On an 8-bit fixture they are never finer than one DMX step.
  • Rows it works on: the Focus row, and the rows that are one row across models (next section).

What you see is the value actually sent. FINE is the same as FINE on Home (chapter 04). Leave it on and go back to Home, and the faders stay fine too.

Pan and Tilt

How Pan and Tilt read depends on the fixture data.

  • Models whose data carries angles: they read in degrees.
  • Most models whose data has no angles: they read in degrees too, using the maker's GDTF values or an assumed Pan of 540° and Tilt of 270°. These can differ from the real fixture.
  • Anything else: reads in percent.

On a 16-bit fixture, coarse and fine sit on one row. Work a row as follows.

  • Drag near the handle and it moves by the distance your finger travels. Anywhere else scrolls the panel.
  • Type an angle into the field. Values outside the fixture's range are refused.
  • Step with ±0.1°, ±1°, ±10° and so on. The steps come from the unit and the resolution.
  • Hold the row's Home button to send it to the fixture's own start position. Let go early to cancel.

With more than one fixture selected and their values different, the slider and the step keys move them all by the same amount. The gaps between them are kept, and the ones that reach an end stop there while the rest carry on. Typing a value, Home, and picking from a list put every fixture on the same value.

FAN sits on the Pan and Tilt rows whenever more than one fixture is selected. Turn it on and the slider sets how far the fixtures fan out: the middle stays where it is and the two ends open out by the same amount, reading ±n°. Turn it off and the slider goes back to moving them together.

Invert Pan and Invert Tilt reverse the direction of Move effects on this fixture only; the slider and the angle it shows are not reversed. On a locked fixture both are dimmed and cannot be switched.

Dead ranges, where the DMX value does nothing, are skipped by both the slider and the steps. On a fixture whose default sits inside a dead range, the steps will not move: use the slider or type a value to get into the live range first.

Position is recorded in HISTORY. Whether it also goes into the current Scene follows chapter 08.

  • AUTO UPDATE: writes it as you work.
  • MANUAL UPDATE: waits for UPDATE.
  • A Scene with Lock This Scene on: records nothing.
IMPORTANT

A Scene fade moves Pan, Tilt and the optics. They travel over the fade time the same way intensity does. What still switches the moment you recall is the values you choose rather than dial — gobo, prism, an animation wheel — and anything set in seconds or hertz. Chapter 08 has the list.

Zoom, iris, frost, focus and gobo

The sections in MOVE are POSITION, GOBO, BEAM, FOCUS and SHAPERS. How you work a row depends on the kind of value.

  • A continuous value: has a slider with the word for each end under it, step keys, and a field to type into.
  • A named choice (a gobo, a prism, an animation wheel): sits between two arrow keys that walk the list one at a time. A long list carries a magnifier to search.

A continuous value such as zoom or frost is one row, even when the models differ.

  • Units: when every selected fixture has the value in the same unit (degrees or m), the row uses that unit. Otherwise it is a percent of each fixture's own range.
  • Slider and typed values: set every fixture to the same value. A fixture whose range does not reach stops at its own end, and the number stopped shows between the end words, such as 1 of 4 at end.
  • Step keys: move each fixture by the same amount from its own value.

These stay as rows for each model and mode.

  • Pan and Tilt
  • Anything chosen by name, such as a gobo or a prism
  • Anything a fixture has more than once, such as the shutter blades
  • Every row, while DMX is selected

Home beside a row sends that one channel to the fixture's own start position. Anything outside these sections is under Channels (chapter 06).

To animate any of it, use Move and Beam in the EFFECT panel. Move works around wherever the head is pointing now, and layers on top of intensity effects.

Saving with a name

Each section — Position, Gobo, Beam, Focus and Shapers — carries its own row of saved values under its heading, each under a name, with SAVE at the end of the row. Each saved name holds its own value for each fixture, not one value shared by all of them.

  1. Select the fixtures and set them the way you want them.
  2. Tap SAVE. A Name box opens with a name already in it, such as POSITION 1.
  3. Tap Save in that box, or change the name first.

SAVE is only there while the selection holds a fixture with rows in that section.

Tapping a name puts the stored values back. They go to the following.

  • With fixtures selected: the fixtures you have selected that were saved under that name.
  • With nothing selected: every fixture saved under it.

A fixture that was not saved under it is left alone. So is one now in a different DMX mode from the one it was saved in.

Hold a name for Rename, Update — which writes what is set now into it — and Delete.

Values saved under a name belong to the show, not to a Scene. Tapping one puts the values there at once; store them in a Scene if you want them to travel over a fade time.

Next
  • Animating movement → chapter 09
  • Storing the whole stage → chapter 08
↑ Contents

08 Storing and recalling looks — Scenes

A Scene is a stored look. Open Scenes, tap SAVE to store, tap a row to bring it back.

Storing a Scene

  1. Set intensity, color and any effects on Home.
  2. Tap Scenes → SAVE. It is stored straight away and becomes the current Scene. While a fade is running, from the recall until it has landed, SAVE is dim and stores nothing.
  3. To rename it, tap Settings on that Scene's row and type a name.
  4. To protect what is in it, turn on Lock This Scene in the same panel.

The Settings here is the one inside the Scene's row. It is not the Settings tab at the bottom of the screen.

SAVE names a new Scene with the whole number after the last numbered one in the list: after 1, 1.1 and 2 it is 3, and with none it is 1. A name is 8 characters at most; a number at its start, such as 12 or 1.25 followed by a space, does not count toward the 8.

When your changes are recorded

Under AUTO UPDATE, the starting setting, whatever you touch after recalling a Scene is written into that Scene at once.

Two buttons at the top of Scenes decide this. A line under them says what the one you picked does.

Until a Scene has been recalled or stored with SAVE, nothing is recorded, and the line says so. The same applies when the recalled Scene is locked.

The choice is kept in the show file rather than on the phone, so a finished show opens the way you left it.

ButtonWhat happens once you have recalled a Scene
AUTO UPDATEEverything you then do to the light is recorded into that Scene as you lift your finger. There is nothing to press
MANUAL UPDATENothing is recorded until you tap UPDATE. Recalling another Scene throws away what you have not recorded, and does not ask

Switching between the two records nothing by itself. Going from MANUAL UPDATE to AUTO UPDATE does not write what is already waiting; AUTO UPDATE starts from your next move.

Under the current Scene's row, a strip says which of these is happening. The strip stays in the same position, and its label and appearance show whether UPDATE can be pressed.

StripWhenTap
LOCKED, greenThe Scene is locked, under either buttonNo
● RECORDING, the dot red and breathingAUTO UPDATE, not lockedNo. It is saying that what you do now is going in
UPDATE, dimMANUAL UPDATE, nothing differs from the recallNo
UPDATE, bright and blinkingMANUAL UPDATE, something differsYes. Records the current state

Under MANUAL UPDATE, UPDATE lights only when something differs from the moment of the recall, or of storing it with SAVE.

  • Take a fader to 30 and back to 50 and there is nothing left to record.
  • While a fade is running, only what you touch is counted, and it goes into the Scene the fade is heading for; values the fade itself is moving are never counted.
  • A FLASH, piano key or HIT you are holding is not recorded; SAVE, UPDATE and AUTO UPDATE record the look as it would be without that press.
  • Lifting your finger from the ZEN fader, or switching TILT off, counts as letting go of a fader.

What a Scene has recorded is not part of HISTORY.

Recalling and tidying

A recall never moves GM, B.O. or ⏻. A Scene does not store them, so a recall cannot raise the grand master, clear a blackout or turn a fixture back on.

There is no way to read what a Scene has stored before you recall it. Its Settings hold the name, the Delay, the fade time, the Curve, Fixture Times, the lock and Delete, and nothing else.

Stepping back repairs a recall; it does not stand in for checking first. The recall counts as one step in HISTORY, and stepping back restores what was there before — only locks are never undone (chapter 10) — but by then the light has already moved, on stage as well as on screen.

Only Fixture Lock or FREE keeps a fixture out of a recall, and a Scene never changes either one (chapter 10 and FREE below). How fast a change is seen depends on what it is: the Fade section below says which values travel over the fade time and which switch at once.

Action or markWhat it does
Tap a rowRecalls when you lift your finger. While Select Many is on, it selects the row instead
NEXT / BACKThe next or previous Scene. It wraps around. Unavailable with only one Scene (see below the table)
● and an amber backgroundThe current Scene
▸The Scene NEXT will bring up. Shown only while a Scene is current
LOCKED and a green edgeLocked against recording
SettingsName, Delay, fade time, Curve, Fixture Times, lock, delete
STAGEOpens the full-screen page for sending Scenes on the night. Shown only with two or more Scenes
Select ManyAt the right edge, under BACK / NEXT. Reorder, and select rows for Copy or Delete (see below the table)
RENUMBERJust left of Select Many. Asks Renumber Scenes?, then with Renumber All numbers every Scene 1, 2, 3 and so on in list order. Not shown while BLIND is on, nor to a guest
CopyCopies each selected Scene to just after itself and any copies already made from it
DeleteAsks first. Copy does not, because nothing is lost. A deleted Scene's MIDI Note goes with it

Notes on the table:

  • NEXT / BACK pressed in quick succession: a press within 0.5 seconds of the one before is ignored, wherever it comes from.
  • Where NEXT / BACK carry on from: after you deselect a Scene or delete it, they carry on from its place in the list.
  • Select Many: it turns into Done, filled amber like SAVE. It is not shown while BLIND is on, nor to a guest that cannot touch Scenes.

Each row of the list shows these.

  • The number: display order.
  • The time under the name: when its contents last changed.
  • At the right of the row: its fade time, such as Fade 3.0s. When the Scene has a Delay, a second line below it reads, for example, Delay 0.6s.

While a Scene is coming in, a bar under its row moves. It runs pale through the Delay, then amber over the fade, moving along the Scene's Curve. The fade time at the right counts down what is left in tenths of a second.

On iPad the row of buttons along the bottom of Home ends with the Scenes. With no Scene yet it is an empty gray strip that reads Scenes you save will appear here.

PartWhat it does
Lock keyLocks the row again
NameThe current Scene's name, with NEXT → and the next one under it. What it shows during a fade is below the table
BACK / NEXTThe same as BACK / NEXT in the Scenes panel
UPDATEReads LOCKED, RECORDING or UPDATE, like the strip under the current Scene's row (see below the table)

Notes on the table:

  • Name: while a Scene fades in, a thin line along the bottom of the name moves. It runs pale through the Delay, then amber over the Fade. The countdown sits beside it.
  • UPDATE: tap RECORDING, or a dim UPDATE, to choose AUTO UPDATE or MANUAL UPDATE from a short list. They cannot be chosen while BLIND is on.

The row is locked each time Kanau opens, with a cover over it from the key to UPDATE. Touching the covered row only shakes it.

  1. Slide the slider on the cover to the right to unlock.
  2. Tap the key to lock it again.

Strap Lock locks it as well, and unlocking Strap Lock leaves it locked.

A copy is named after its source's number with one more decimal.

  • 1 gives 1.1, then 1.2 up to 1.9. 1.1 gives 1.11.
  • Only the number is carried, not the rest of the name.
  • A source with no number gives the smallest whole number not in use.

A copy keeps the contents, the Delay, the fade time, the Curve and Fixture Times. It is never locked, even when the one it came from is.

The copies become the selected rows, so pressing Copy again copies the copies.

RENUMBER changes names only. The number goes in front of the name.

  • Opening becomes 1 Opening.
  • A number already there is replaced, so 1.1 Toast becomes 2 Toast.
  • An empty name becomes the number alone.

The order, the current Scene and what is recorded stay as they are. The old numbers cannot be brought back, and HISTORY does not hold them.

Play — stepping through Scenes from Home (iPhone)

Tap Play in the tabs at the bottom, then PLAY in the list that opens. No panel opens: the bottom row becomes the Play row, and Home stays in view. The current Scene's number and name sit at the top left of the row (the name in amber, or the mark — with nothing recalled), with low EXIT and UPDATE buttons under them. A thin line along the top of the row follows the fade.

ButtonWhat it does
EXITPuts the usual buttons back
UPDATEThe same as UPDATE under the current Scene's row. Under AUTO UPDATE it reads ● RECORDING. While BLIND is on, it records the BLIND look
BACK / NEXTThe previous or next Scene, as in Scenes

BACK and NEXT only vibrate, and the Scene does not move, while you hold a fader, when there is only one Scene, and on a guest that can only watch. On iPad the Play list has no PLAY; the Scenes in the row along the bottom of Home do the same job.

COMMAND — work by typing numbers

Tap Play in the tabs at the bottom, then COMMAND in the list that opens, and the command entry panel opens. On iPad it is in the Play list in the column on the left. A guest that is not allowed to control has no COMMAND.

Type fixture numbers to select fixtures or set their intensity and color temperature. However many fixtures there are, picking them takes the same few keys.

What you type shows at the top. The line under it says what ENTER will do, such as 4 fixtures → 50%. ENTER carries it out.

  • When it works: the line clears and you can type the next one.
  • When it does not: you get a warning vibration and nothing changes.

Each ENTER is one step in HISTORY.

The keys

The keys are in 5 columns, based on the grandMA3 layout.

  • Row 1: COLOR, EFFECT, ZEN, (empty), ⌫
  • Row 2: GROUP, 7, 8, 9, +
  • Row 3: SCENE, 4, 5, 6, THRU
  • Row 4: FIXTURE, 1, 2, 3, −
  • Row 5: (empty), 0, ., K, AT
  • Row 6: STORE, ENTER (two keys wide), CLEAR, FULL

Keys that pick fixtures (GROUP, FIXTURE, THRU, +, −) are amber; keys for values and actions are light blue. ⌫ removes one key. CLEAR clears what you typed and the fixture selection; it does not change any intensity.

The SELECTED line under what you type shows the current selection, written the way you would type it, such as 1 THRU 10 + 15 · 11 fixtures. With nothing selected it shows —.

Numbers

Every number is a fixture number (the Fixture Number, chapter 03). FIXTURE can be left out: FIXTURE 5 and 5 are the same.

100.3 is pixel 3 of fixture 100, counting pixels in the order they appear on screen.

Selecting

Type only numbers and press ENTER, and the fixtures are selected, nothing more. COLOR, EFFECT and the rest then work on them as usual.

TypeSelects
5 / 1 + 3 + 7Fixture 5 / fixtures 1, 3 and 7
1 THRU 50 / 50 THRU 1Fixtures 1 to 50. Typed backwards, the order is reversed, and so is the direction values are spread in
1 THRU 50 − 251 to 50 without 25
100.1 THRU 100.8Pixels 1 to 8 of fixture 100
100.5 THRU 102.3From pixel 5 of fixture 100 to pixel 3 of fixture 102, across fixtures
100 − 100.3Every pixel of fixture 100 except pixel 3
GROUP 2 / GROUP 2 + 5The group whose name starts with 2 (chapter 03) / that group plus fixture 5
+ 9 / − 9Adds fixture 9 to the current selection / removes it
GROUP 1 THRU 3Groups 1 to 3 together, in the order typed. − takes fixtures out
. 3 / . 1 THRU 4Pixel 3 / pixels 1 to 4 of each fixture selected now. Select the fixtures first. 1 THRU 10 . 3 reads as 10.3, pixel 3 of fixture 10

Setting values

TypeWhat happens
1 THRU 10 AT 50Sets them to 50%
AT 50Sets the selected fixtures to 50%
. 2 AT 50Sets pixel 2 of each selected fixture to 50%
AT + 10 / AT − 20Raises them by 10 / lowers them by 20, each from its own level
1 THRU 10 AT 0 THRU 100Spreads 0 to 100 across them in the order typed
1 THRU 5 AT 0 THRU 100 THRU 0THRU can go on as many times as you like. Values are spread in straight lines between the ones typed, so this gives 0, 50, 100, 50, 0
FULL / AT FULLSets 100%
AT 5600 KSets the color temperature to 5600 K
AT 2700 THRU 6500 KSpreads color temperature from 2700 K to 6500 K. One K at the end is enough
1 THRU 20 COLORSelects them and opens the COLOR panel. EFFECT and ZEN work the same way. Adding AT, as in 1 + 2 + 3 AT EFFECT, does the same
1 THRU 50 STORE GROUP 4Makes group 4 from them. STORE GROUP alone uses the next free number. An existing number is never written over
SCENE 5 / SCENE 1.1Recalls the Scene with that number

After an ENTER that sends a value (AT 50, FULL, AT + 10, AT 5600 K and so on) and after STORE GROUP, the selection is cleared. An ENTER that only selects, and opening COLOR, EFFECT or ZEN, keep it.

The line before ENTER

ShowsMeaning
4 fixtures → 50%Four fixtures will go to 50%
IncompleteThe line is not finished
Out of rangeAn intensity outside 0 to 100, such as AT 500. It is not turned into 100
Not found: 999There is no fixture with that number
2 lockedTwo locked fixtures will not move
2 no CCTTwo fixtures have no color temperature and will not move
2 no pxA pixel number was typed for fixtures without pixels
