Not on this deviceIt does not work on this device

Limits

  • Intensity is 0 to 100 only, and stays within each fixture's limits. Locked fixtures do not move.
  • Color temperature stays within each fixture's range.
  • On a guest, intensity and color temperature are sent to the host and take effect there. STORE GROUP and SCENE do not work.
  • During BLIND, STORE GROUP does not work.

REVERT — back to how the Scene was when you recalled it

Under AUTO UPDATE a Scene changes as you work. REVERT puts it back to how it was when you recalled it, or stored it with SAVE.

  1. Recall a Scene and work the light. Under AUTO UPDATE, or after UPDATE, the Scene changes.
  2. REVERT appears beside RECORDING or UPDATE, under the current Scene's row.
  3. Tap it. Revert Scene? asks first; tap REVERT.

The Scene's look goes back, and the light then fades to it over the Scene's fade, as a recall does. GM, B.O. and ⏻ do not move, and neither do locked fixtures. The name, the times, the Curve, Fixture Times and the lock stay as they are.

  • REVERT is not shown on a locked Scene, or while the Scene matches the moment you recalled it, and it is not on the iPad's row along the bottom of Home. Under MANUAL UPDATE it appears only after UPDATE has changed the Scene.
  • Deselecting the Scene, deleting it or opening another show clears the point REVERT goes back to.
  • The light's move is one step in HISTORY, but the Scene's contents are not: UNDO puts the light back and leaves the Scene reverted.
  • In BLIND, the Scene is reverted and only the copy recalls it; the lights do not move. A guest that can only watch does not see REVERT.

FREE — fixtures a Scene leaves alone

A FREE fixture is skipped by Scene recalls: the list, NEXT, BACK, STAGE, Play and MIDI leave it where it is, during a fade as well. Faders, the piano and HISTORY still move it, and GM, B.O. and BATTERY SAVE still apply.

  1. Hold the fixture's round icon.
  2. On the panel's SETUP tab, the FREE section under Lock has one button. It reads Not FREE or FREE, or n of m FREE when several fixtures are mixed. Tap it to switch; when they are mixed, a tap clears FREE on all of them. It is amber while FREE is on.

A FREE fixture carries an F on its round icon, and now and then the status line shows the count, such as FREE ×3. A fixture is FREE or locked, never both. AUTO UPDATE and UPDATE leave a FREE fixture's stored value in the Scene as it was; SAVE stores its present value in the new Scene. The FREE master on the GM panel scales all FREE fixtures together (chapter 04).

STAGE — sending Scenes on the night

STAGE is a full-screen page for sending Scenes during the show, on a black background.

  • To open it: tap STAGE in the title row of Scenes, to the left of SAVE, or STAGE in the Play list.
  • When it is shown: only when there are two or more Scenes and BLIND is off. A guest in a session that can only watch does not see it.
PartWhat it does
Settings mark, top rightOpens STAGE settings, described under this table
×, top leftLeaves STAGE and returns to Scenes
The name above NEXTThe current Scene, written large, with an amber ● at its left while a Scene is current. Until a Scene is recalled it reads —
NEXT and BACKThe two large buttons. Each shows the name and fade time of the Scene it goes to (see below the table)

Notes on the table:

  • Inside NEXT: ▸ and the next Scene's name with its fade time (Fade 3.0s, or Fade 3.0s Delay 0.6s when the Scene has a Delay).
  • Inside BACK: ◂ and the previous Scene's name with its fade time.
  • Size: BACK is half as tall as NEXT, and the same width.

You can see where each goes before you press it.

The mark at the top right opens STAGE settings, with Done at its top right. Buttons chooses one of these.

  • NEXT: the whole page below the name is one NEXT button.
  • BACK + NEXT: BACK is above NEXT.

The choice is kept on this device, and BACK + NEXT is the default.

The Scene goes out when you lift your finger, so sliding off a button before you let go sends nothing.

  • After the last Scene: NEXT goes round to the first, with a warning vibration.
  • Pressed in quick succession: a press within 0.5 seconds of the one before is refused, with the same warning vibration. A hand that lands twice does not send two Scenes. The same holds for every NEXT and BACK.
  • Screen lock: while STAGE is open the screen does not lock itself, either by tilting the phone or through iOS.

BLIND — working without touching the lights

BLIND, the wide button under the title of Scenes, starts a copy of the console whose changes do not reach the lights. A line under it says what it does. While BLIND is on, the button is amber with a light running along it.

The copy starts from the faders, colors and effects as they are, or from where a running fade is heading. The lights keep doing what they were doing.

The band at the top, the edge of the screen and each panel are marked in amber. Nothing you do in BLIND goes into HISTORY.

While BLIND is onWhat
Change the copy onlyFaders, color, effects, Scene recalls
Still act on the lightsGM, B.O.
RecordSAVE stores the BLIND look as a new Scene; UPDATE writes it into the current one (see below the table)
ClosedPatch, Output, Session, Shows, HISTORY, Scene settings. In a fixture's panel the name cannot be typed and Label Color, BATTERY SAVE, Invert and Switch are hidden
Open, and realREORDER on Home. It changes the order of the show itself, not only of the copy, and its move is a step in HISTORY

Notes on the table:

  • How it records: BLIND always records the way MANUAL UPDATE does. AUTO UPDATE and MANUAL UPDATE are not shown.
  • UPDATE on iPhone: UPDATE is also on Home, in the place of BATTERY SAVE, and now and then shows the current Scene's name. While the Play row is showing, use UPDATE there.

To leave, tap BLIND again, or BLIND at the top left of the screen. With unsaved changes it asks Update, Save New, Discard or Cancel. Leaving never changes the lights. A guest in a session has no BLIND.

Scene Lock

Turn on Lock This Scene for Scenes you want left alone. You can still recall them and still work the light, but nothing is recorded. LOCKED is shown on every locked row, not only on the current one.

Lock is stronger than either AUTO UPDATE or MANUAL UPDATE. A locked Scene never says RECORDING.

This is not the same as Fixture Lock. Scene Lock protects what is stored; Fixture Lock holds the output.

What is stored, and what is not

A Scene stores intensities, colors, positions and effects. It does not store the grand master, B.O. or ⏻. The table below says exactly what.

Stored and brought backNot stored
Intensity, CCT, G/M, crossfade, RGB, emitters, the name of the gel picked from a tableGM and B.O.
Raw channels such as position and gobo, cell color and intensity, effects⏻ state, BATTERY SAVE, Power Switch
Color groupsLimits, Fixture Lock, FREE, group masters

Locks and limits belong to the console, not to a Scene. A Scene does not record them and a recall does not apply them.

  • A recall: it never locks, unlocks or re-limits a fixture. The console's limits apply to every Scene.
  • A locked fixture's value: AUTO UPDATE and UPDATE do not write it and leave the value the Scene already has. SAVE takes its present value. A FREE fixture is treated the same way.
  • When you unlock a fixture: nothing moves. The next recall brings in the Scene's value.

Fade

Set the fade time per Scene, in the Scene's Settings → Fade. 3 seconds is the default.

  • Buttons: six preset buttons, SNAP, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2 and 3, and ±0.1 and ±1 to adjust. The button times cannot be changed.
  • Any other time: type it in the boxed field beside the heading. Tap it, type the seconds on the number keys and press Return.
  • Range: the same as the ± buttons, 0 to 600 seconds in steps of 0.1, so typing 700 gives 600. Something that cannot be read as a number changes nothing.

The Scene's Settings open over the whole screen, with × at the top left. These are the parts that set the fade.

  • The bar at the top: shows the Delay as a dotted line and the Fade after it. Drag the knob where they meet for the Delay and the one at the end for the Fade, in steps of 0.1 seconds.
  • Delay: under the bar. It is how long the whole Scene waits after the recall before anything moves. It is 0 unless you set it. It has the same ± keys and a boxed field to type the seconds, but no preset buttons.
  • Curve: under Fade. It sets how the fade moves: S-CURVE, the default, starts and lands gently; EASE IN starts gently only; LINEAR moves at one even speed.

Settings → Settings → Fade Times → Scene Curve sets the Curve for every Scene at once, and for Scenes saved from now on.

These values travel over the fade time.

  • Intensity, color, cell values and color groups
  • Pan, Tilt and the continuous beam values such as Zoom, Focus and Iris
  • Amber, White, Lime, the fixture's own Hue and Saturation, x and y, and CMY

They follow the Scene's Curve. Hue goes the short way round the circle. The faders move with them.

What you touch partway through a fade — with a fader, ⏻, color or a MIDI knob, or from a guest in a session — leaves the fade and stays where you put it, while the fixture's other values carry on; just taking hold of a fader is enough. Under AUTO UPDATE what you touched goes into the Scene the fade is heading for at once; under MANUAL UPDATE, UPDATE lights.

A piano key or FLASH gives its value while held and is not recorded; let go and the fixture stops at the value it had before you pressed, then goes to the Scene's value when the fade lands. A key still held when the fade lands goes to the Scene's value when you let go.

These do not interpolate. They switch to the stored value the moment you recall, whatever the fade time says.

  • A fader set as a switch, and the name of the gel
  • The raw values that are chosen rather than dialed: gobo, prism, an animation wheel
  • Anything set in seconds or hertz

An effect you start, stop or change during the fade is yours and stays as you set it. If the look you are coming from holds no position at all (an older Scene, for example), the head lands on the new value at once.

Effects cross over with the fade, along the Scene's Curve.

  • An effect the Scene brings: starts when its fixture starts to move and grows from nothing over that fixture's Fade.
  • An effect the Scene does not have: keeps running while it fades out, and is released when the fade lands.
  • Where both have one: the light passes from the old to the new.
  • What switches at once: an effect that plays once, ONE FIRE, the SIGNAL crossings and a recall with a fade of 0.

For a fixture that has a Delay (see Fixture Times below), effects reach it when its Delay ends.

The recall itself is recorded in HISTORY as one step. Scenes are part of the show file.

Fixture Times — a different time for each fixture

Every fixture follows the Scene's Fade unless you say otherwise. Fixture Times, in the Scene's Settings below Fade, gives chosen fixtures times of their own.

  • Delay: the fixture starts at a time of its own, counted from the recall.
  • Fade: the fixture takes its own time to get there.

This lets a look build across the stage. The section is not shown while there are no fixtures.

A fixture you have not set follows the Scene's Delay and Fade. One set to a Delay of 0 starts at the recall even when the Scene has a Delay.

Beside the heading, in amber, is the time until the last fixture has arrived: the longest Delay plus Fade among the fixtures.

A short explanation and a scale in seconds follow, then one row for each fixture, in fader order. Each row has the fixture's number in thin type, its name and a bar.

  • The name: sits on the fixture's Label Color when it has one.
  • The bar: a dotted line is the Delay, and the bar after it is the Fade. A Fade of 0 shows as a thin vertical mark where the fixture starts.
  • How strong the bar is: stronger for a fixture that has a time of its own, paler for one that follows the Scene's Fade.

The scale is fixed by the Scene's Fade: the width you can see holds at least 5 seconds, and at least twice the Scene's Fade. Giving one fixture a long Delay or Fade does not shrink the bars of the others; only the bar of the long fixture grows. To see what runs past the edge, slide the band sideways with a finger; the scale and all the bars move together. The column of names stays still.

Drag the knob at the start of a fixture's bar to set its Delay, and the one at the end to set its Fade. The fixture then has times of its own. Touching a knob without moving it changes nothing.

Dragging the knob of a selected fixture moves every selected fixture by the same amount, keeping the differences between them. One that reaches 0 stops there while the others carry on, as faders do on Home.

A row under the explanation narrows the list and stays at the top while you scroll.

  • Fixtures | Groups: at the left of the row. It switches between a button for each model and ALL with a button for each group.
  • Holding a button: selects every fixture in it.
  • Tapping a row: selects it; tap it again to let it go. A selected row has a thick amber edge.
  • Pressing another group button: lets go of the rows it hides.

While anything is selected, a bar appears at the bottom of the panel.

  • What it holds: the number selected out of all the fixtures, RESET and CLEAR, and a line each for Delay and Fade.
  • The value on each line: the value of the selected fixtures, or — when they differ.
  • −1, −0.1, +0.1 and +1: change every selected fixture by that much from its own present value, so the differences between them stay.

Delay and Fade stay within the same range as the Scene's own Fade.

Tap the value on the Delay or Fade line to type it. The number keys open, and Return gives every selected fixture exactly that number, not a step from its own value. Something that cannot be read as a number changes nothing.

  • RESET: sends the selected fixtures back to the Scene's Delay and Fade.
  • CLEAR: lets go of every selected row, as CLEAR does on Home. The bottom bar closes and the times stay as they are.

On a recall, a fixture that has a Delay stays as it was until its Delay ends, then moves over its own Fade. The Scene's effects come to each fixture at the moment it starts.

  • Repeating effects on the light: keep time with the recall, so fixtures that started late still blink and chase in step.
  • Effects on position and beam, and effects that play once: begin from rest at the moment that fixture starts.
  • SIGNAL crossings: switch when the Scene's Delay ends, or at once when there is none.

What you touch on a fixture that is still waiting leaves the fade and stays as you set it. An effect you change during the fade is not overwritten when a waiting fixture's Delay ends.

The NEXT row in a fixture's panel

Hold a round icon, and the SETUP tab of its panel has a NEXT row under the Fade Time heading: the Delay and Fade this fixture takes into the Scene NEXT will bring up.

  • Tap a value and type the seconds. With several fixtures, every one of them takes the number you type; — shows while they differ.
  • A fixture with no time of its own shows the Scene's time, dimmed. Typing gives it a time of its own, and RESET sends it back to the Scene's.
  • The row is shown only while a Scene is current. A guest that cannot touch Scenes sees the values only.
  • On iPad, when the panel is in two columns, NEXT, Delay, Fade and RESET sit on one line.

09 Effects

Blink, fire, lightning and the rest, applied to your fixtures.

EFFECT on Home is the way in. What it opens depends on whether fixtures are selected.

  • With fixtures selected: it opens the effect panel for them.
  • With nothing selected: it opens the list of everything that is running. There, effects are released, paused and cleared. An effect can also be chosen first and its fixtures picked next.

Holding a round icon on Home opens that fixture's own panel, and EFFECT sits there too, to the right of ZEN. It opens the effect panel for that fixture.

Applying one

  1. On Home, tap the round icon of a fixture or a cell to select it.
  2. Open EFFECT.
  3. Tap an effect name. It starts immediately.

To choose the effect first, tap EFFECT with nothing selected, then EFFECT under Applies To in the list. Tap a name and a panel opens under it to pick its fixtures; Done starts it. Cancel, or pulling the panel down, starts nothing.

The fader still sets intensity. While an effect runs, the fixture icon and fader move with it. The EFFECT button changes as follows.

  • With its fixtures selected: it carries the effect's name, or PAUSED while it is paused.
  • With nothing selected: it reads N RUNNING, such as 2 RUNNING.

On a fader set as a switch, intensity effects do nothing. Color effects still change its color.

At the top of the panel, a round icon stands for each step. Each icon shows the movement it is actually making.

  • Color: the color of the light source in the step.
  • Number: the step's number in the order, underneath. It is not the fixture number.
  • Empty step: a step with nothing in it is a faint ring carrying +. It stays dark as the chase goes past.

The band above the icons shows the shape over time. It is in the effect's own color when the effect carries one, and plain when it does not.

Under the icons sit three buttons: TOGETHER, SPREAD and STEPS.

  • TOGETHER: moves every light source as one.
  • SPREAD: gives each light source its own place in the run. Spread in Arrange sets how far apart.
  • STEPS: lit once you have set the steps by hand. When Kanau deals out the steps itself, it stays dark.

Of TOGETHER and SPREAD, the lit one shows the current state. With nothing selected, the one you press is kept for the effect you apply next.

The movement and the steps are two different settings, so two buttons can be lit at once (SPREAD over three steps, for example). RUNNER, FADE RUN and COMET always run apart.

STEPS opens the page for editing the steps. It covers every fixture running that effect, not only the ones selected. So a change to the steps keeps the whole chase in step.

  • Rows: each step is a row. It shows what is in the step (Empty when there is nothing) and a SELECT of its own.
  • + ADD STEP: adds one step on the end.
  • EDIT: brings out the handles. Drag a row by its handle to move it to another place in the order.
  • DELETE: swipe a row to the left to show it.

One step is the fewest there can be. One step is TOGETHER.

Tapping an empty step opens the fixture list. It is the same one the step list's SELECT opens. Whatever is already in that step is ticked.

  1. Tick the fixtures to put in the step, and untick the ones to take out.
  2. Tap Done to confirm.

Cancel, or pulling the panel down, leaves the step as it was.

Tap the icons to pick out fixtures. The row under them says how many are MARKED. ALL marks every one and CLEAR lets them go.

An icon marked … opens that fixture's own color and intensity panel on a hold. It is the same panel as the round icon on Home. Hold with several picked out and they open together.

Pause, release, restart

ActionWhat it does
BACKGoes back one step. With TOGETHER it goes back a whole cycle
NEXTGoes on one step, the same way
PAUSEFreezes the movement at the current intensity and position
RESUMECarries on from where it froze
RELEASEStops it and hands control back to the normal values. The settings stay in the list
STARTRuns a released effect again from the beginning
CLEARRemoves it from the list. It asks first

BACK and NEXT are the two arrow buttons at the left of the row. They move while the effect is paused as well, so you can walk through it a step at a time. While something runs, the button at the right of the row says RELEASE. Once it is released, the same button says START, so the effect can be set going again without leaving the panel.

The panel draws the waveform in its running shape even when the effect is paused or released. So the top left of the waveform shows the state.

  • PAUSED: the effect is paused. Only the movement stops; the light stays on.
  • RELEASED: the effect is released. The light is back to its own look.
  • No label: nothing shows while the effect runs.

An effect takes 0.5 s to come in when you press it and 0.5 s to go out when you stop it. The fires take 3 s to come in and 4 s to go out. This time is used in these cases.

  • Pressing an effect's button, choosing a saved setting, or stopping an effect
  • Pressing RELEASE and START, or RELEASE ALL and START ALL
  • Switching TOGETHER and SPREAD, the arrangement, Runs, Direction or CYCLE while the effect runs
  • Adding, deleting or reordering steps in STEPS

Recalling a Scene uses the Scene's own fade. ONE FIRE and SIGNAL switch at once.

Adjust

ItemWhat it is
SpeedIn hertz. Decimals allowed. TAP is at the right of the reading. Not on Move, Beam or SIGNAL
EnergyOn some kinds, one knob in place of the others. It moves Speed, Depth and the rest together
DepthHow far down it pulls the intensity. 100 reaches zero; 35 barely moves
SizeOn the kinds that move the head, in place of Depth. How far it swings, in degrees per axis. FINE beside it works like FINE on Home
How OftenHow often it happens. The same knob reads Crossing Time on PASS and Saturation on RAINBOW. Only on the kinds that use it
ShapeOn ORBIT, EIGHT, BOX, SPIRAL and SEARCH. At 50% the shape is as drawn; lower flattens it toward a swing from side to side, higher toward up and down
GlideOn JUMP. At 0 it jumps at each step; higher, it travels to the next point over that share of the step
RoughnessHow ragged the wander is, on the five fires, WATER, LANTERNS, DRIFT, HANDHELD, WIND and BALLYHOO
WidthHow much of the rig is lit at once, for example 50% 2 / 4. On one fixture, or with TOGETHER, how long each beat stays lit
TailThe length of COMET's tail
RandomHow much the beat and the height wander. 0 keeps it regular
DramaOn the five fires. 0 is the real thing; higher makes it a stage fire. It is under Advanced, with the other single knobs

Which items appear depends on the effect. SIGNAL has a panel of its own instead.

Notes on the table:

  • TAP on Speed: takes the beat. Tap it four times in time and every running light effect on unlocked fixtures follows that beat. Each runs at the number of cycles to a beat that suits it. A gap of more than two seconds starts the count again.
  • Kinds with Energy: the five fires (CANDLE, TORCH, FIREPLACE, CAMPFIRE and BONFIRE). Also WATER, TOKYO, OSAKA, KYOTO, NARA, FLUO FLICKER and FLUO RESTART.
  • Energy's starting value and the single knobs: CANDLE, KYOTO and WATER start at 75%, BONFIRE at 70%, the others at 50%. The single knobs are under Advanced. One you move there keeps its own value.
  • Angles in Size: ±25.2° / ±12.6° swings both ways, and 0–45° goes one way. A single moving axis is named, as in Pan 0–90°. The biggest shapes reach ±90°.
  • Speed in Size: beside the angle is the fastest the head moves, such as 158°/s. For LIGHTHOUSE this includes the run-up at the start of each swing.
  • 8-bit heads: when the shape is under 16 steps, 8-bit 2.1°/step under Size shows the angle of one step. The values sent do not change.
  • Shape on SEARCH: it sets the direction of the swing. 50% is across, and 0% or 100% is up and down.
  • Width above 50%: PULSE and FADE RUN hold flat at the top.

ROLES — which lights are which color (BEACON R/B)

BEACON R/B starts with TOGETHER, and its panel carries ROLES under Adjust. There is a button for each role, such as ● RED 2, ● BLUE 2 and ● WHITE 1, with the number of fixtures in it.

  1. Tap a role, such as ● RED. A list opens to pick the lights for it.
  2. Tick the lights and tap Done. Cancel, or pulling the list down, changes nothing.

If you pick none, they split in order: half red, half blue, and lights without color go white.

Arrange

Arrange holds the following, from the top.

  • Spread (or Link)
  • The buttons that only work while held
  • Color Source (AUTO, COLOR, KEEP)
  • ONE FIRE
  • The arrangement

The kinds that only move the head or the beam carry no Color Source. Under the three Color Source buttons, one line for each says what it means, and the one you have chosen is shown bright. So you can tell before pressing which color each will give.

With two or more fixtures, Arrange also carries Spread. It sets how far apart the fixtures run. At 0% they run together, and at 100% they are spread over the whole cycle.

0% is TOGETHER, and moving it up turns SPREAD on. The SPREAD button sets it back to 100%. Spread is on the kinds that run along the rig. It is not on the towns or SIGNAL.

The flickers (the five fires, the two FLUO, WATER, LANTERNS, TV and NEON) carry Link instead. At 0 each fixture flickers on its own. Higher lets the same flicker travel along the order, so that neighbors look alike. 100 makes them one, and on a fire 100 is ONE FIRE.

ColorWhat it does
AUTOThe effect decides. The ones that carry no color of their own leave yours alone
COLORIt runs in the colors you set below. A color appears even on the kinds that have none
KEEPOnly the brightness moves. The color stays as you set it on the fader
ArrangementWhat it does
IN ORDEREvenly staggered by number
ALTERNATEOdd and even, half a cycle apart
WINGSMirrored out from the center. On a moving head the back half also turns Pan the other way, so the two sides swing in and out together
RANDOMIn a random order
BOUNCETurns around at each end
BUILDLights one at a time, then clears them all together
SPELLERLights one at a time, and once they are all on, everything flashes together three times
PASSLike IN ORDER, but fast through the middle and slow at the ends, the way a car goes past

BOUNCE, BUILD and SPELLER are not offered on Move, Beam or RAINBOW.

Some kinds put a button in Arrange that only works while you hold it.

  • FLARE and WIND: on the five fires. Hold FLARE to make the fire flare up, and WIND to let a gust beat it down.
  • HIT: on FLUO FLICKER and FLUO RESTART. On FLUO FLICKER, hold it and the tube fails; let go and it comes back. On FLUO RESTART, each press puts the tube out and lights it again.

With a fire on two or more fixtures, Arrange also carries ONE FIRE. With it on, the fixtures burn as one big flame. Its rise and fall reaches each fixture a little later along their order, while each keeps its own flicker. Turning ONE FIRE on turns TOGETHER off.

CYCLE, on IN ORDER, BOUNCE, BUILD and PASS, is how many steps one cycle spans. Leave it empty to run one cycle across the whole selection. A number in CYCLE wins over Runs, and pressing Runs empties it. It is not shown once the steps are set by hand.

Runs, on the same four, is how many patterns run at once, set with − n +. It will not go past the number of fixtures you have selected.

On PASS, Curve sets how much it slows at the ends. At 0% it moves as evenly as IN ORDER.

Direction is FORWARD or REVERSE.

The STEPS row in Arrange shows how many steps the chase is running over, and how your fixtures or pixels are dealt into them. With more fixtures than steps, a step holds several. With more steps than fixtures, the spare ones stay dark. Press STEPS above to change how many there are, and which fixture sits in which.

INVERT and REPEAT sit under Options, below Arrange.

INVERT swaps the lit and the dark. One step lighting up becomes one step going out, and a chase that fills becomes one that empties.

With REPEAT on, the effect keeps going round. With it off, the effect runs once and holds its last look; press the effect again to run from the start. The five fires have no REPEAT; they always keep burning.

The arrangement, CYCLE, Runs, STEPS and Direction only appear while SPREAD is on, and only on the kinds that run along the rig. INVERT and REPEAT sit outside that: REPEAT is on every kind but the five fires, and INVERT on every kind but RAINBOW.

Both work with TOGETHER as well. Invert a blink set to 20% width and you get a short dip in an otherwise bright look. Invert STROBE and you get short blackouts inside the light. Turn REPEAT off and you get one flash that holds where it ends.

Advanced

Every effect carries an Advanced section below Options. Its heading is amber, because it opens. It stays folded until you open it, and the folded heading says EDITED once you have changed something. Each block in it has a RESET of its own, which returns that block only to its starting values and leaves everything else alone.

BlockOnWhat you change
ColorsBeacons, PACHINKO, FIREWORKS, the towns, LIGHTNING, and any kind set to COLOR in ArrangeEach lamp or flash, by name: RED, BLUE, AMBER and the rest
TubeFLUO FLICKER, FLUO RESTARTMONO or COLOR, and the color of a healthy tube
TemperatureThe five firesLOW and HIGH in kelvin at full fader, in steps of 50
MAXThe five firesHow strongly FLARE and WIND act. 10 to 100%, in steps of 10

Notes on the table:

  • Colors on the towns: FROM and TO are the two ends of the range the street drifts between. Set both the same and the hue goes the whole way round.
  • Colors on LIGHTNING: FAR and NEAR are the far strike and the near one.

This is where you change a fire's own color, because on AUTO it works that color out from its temperature.

Tap a button under Colors to open a page for choosing its color.

  • Color buttons: choose from Color, Gels and Favorites.
  • Color-temperature buttons: such as WHITE on BEACON R/B and FIREWORKS. Choose from CCT and Favorites. A color temperature goes to the fixture's color-temperature channel where it has one.
  • BEACON R/B: the buttons split into COLOR FIXTURES (RED and BLUE) and WHITE FIXTURES (WHITE). Each shows how many fixtures play that part. A part with none is not shown.

A button you have changed carries an amber dot. DEFAULT at the top of its page puts that one back, and RESET for Colors puts them all back.

The towns — TOKYO, OSAKA, KYOTO, NARA

The four towns differ in character, and each has moments of its own that come now and then. Speed on the towns goes up to 3 Hz.

TownWhat it does
TOKYOMany colors, moving fast. Now and then every sign cuts to one color, or the screens flash white
OSAKAStrong primaries, switching hard. Now and then every sign blinks three times
KYOTOWarm and muted. Lanterns, moving slowly. A breeze passes along the row, and now and then someone walks past a light
NARAThe dimmest. Stone lanterns, barely moving. Now and then a cloud dims them all, or one lantern is relit

Each time you apply a town it is a different night. Stop it and press it again, or apply it from the Saved row, and the time of the special moments, the colors it switches to, the order of the people and fires and the colors the signs drift to all come out differently. The town's character stays the same. A Scene remembers the night it was stored with, and recalling it from a different look starts that same night from the beginning.

Changing the target, and saving settings

Applies To → FIXTURES picks fixtures and groups. The selection is shared with Home, and the list stays open while you choose. A model opens into its fixtures, and a fixture with pixels opens again into ALL PIXELS and P1 … Pn.

A fixture goes in whole or by pixel, not both. If both end up chosen, the pixels stay and the whole fixture is let go.

When you select a pixel fixture itself and apply an effect, how it is applied depends on PIXELS on Home.

  • With PIXELS open: it works as if you had selected all of its pixels. The arrangement, Runs and Direction play across the pixels, and the panel counts them. One fixture with 16 pixels reads 16 selected.
  • With PIXELS closed: each fixture is one step.

An effect that is already running keeps the unit it was applied with when you adjust it, whichever way PIXELS is set.

SAVE, at the top right of the panel, stores the settings you have dialed in, under a name. It is always there. When there is nothing to store, it is dimmed and pressing it stores nothing. That is when nothing is running on the selected fixtures, or when different effects are.

The Saved row appears once a setting is stored. It also says why when the effects are mixed or the stored settings cannot be read.

  • Apply: stored settings are listed under SELECT ▾. Pick one to apply it.
  • Stop: pick the ticked one again to stop it.
  • Rename and delete: open EDIT at the bottom of the list and pick the setting. Changes made there stay even if you close it by swiping down. An empty name is refused with Enter a name, and the old name stays.

The fixtures are not part of a stored setting.

Select the fixtures already running along with the new ones, pick the same effect, and the speed, depth and phase carry over. Where the settings differ, the effect falls back to the defaults. To release just one fixture, select only that one and tap RELEASE.

Finding one by what you want

What you wantTry
Natural lightCANDLE, TORCH, FIREPLACE, CAMPFIRE, BONFIRE, LIGHTNING, WATER, TV
Light running along the rigRUNNER, FADE RUN, COMET
City lightNEON, SIGNAL, TOKYO, OSAKA, KYOTO, NARA, PACHINKO
BeaconsBEACON R/B, BEACON BLUE, BEACON RED, BEACON AMBER
Press camerasPAPARAZZI
Plain flashingBLINK, STROBE, PULSE, DOUBLE, JITTER, SPARKLE, RARE FLASH
Color on the moveRAINBOW
A failing fluorescentFLUO FLICKER, FLUO RESTART
Moving the headThe Move group, WIND among them
Moving zoom or goboThe Beam group
An old signMarquee

PAPARAZZI is camera flashes from a crowd. Each fixture fires on its own and stays dark in between, so the more fixtures you give it the less it looks like a pattern. How Often sets how many go off.

The fires, and the failing tubes

There are five fires. The four other than CANDLE are wood fires.

  • CANDLE: a candle. In still air it sits almost still, and it only moves when something disturbs it.
  • TORCH: a torch in the wind, never still, with sparks.
  • FIREPLACE: a fireplace, steady and lively, with no wind.
  • CAMPFIRE: a campfire, slower than the fireplace, with a gust now and then.
  • BONFIRE: a large fire, with slow, deep surges and a gust pushing it down now and then.

Speed goes up to 2.4 Hz on TORCH, 2.2 Hz on FIREPLACE, and 2.5 Hz on CAMPFIRE and BONFIRE. A fire rises from embers when it starts. When it stops, it sinks back to embers before it hands over to the plain light.

Drama sits under Advanced on every fire and starts at 0. 0 is the real thing. Raise it and the fire becomes a stage fire: it stops going still, it reddens as it drops, and it flickers more than a real one would.

The fires take Color Source in Arrange like any other effect.

  • AUTO: the flame's heat sets the color: deep red as it dies down, warmer white as it flares. The temperature is under Advanced.
  • COLOR: they burn in the colors you set below, keeping the flame's shape.
  • KEEP: only the brightness moves. Your color from the faders stays.

The further you pull the fader below half, the more the fire sinks toward the red of embers. When the light drops, the temperature does not drop at once. Each light runs a slightly different color.

On COLOR, each time the fire sinks, your color leans toward its red side. A fire whose LOW and HIGH you have changed never leaves that range.

On AUTO, a fire whose fixtures carry both a color temperature channel and color of their own gets AUTO, CCT and RGB to choose between. Where a fixture has only one of the two, the choice does not appear. CCT and RGB do not reach the same color.

  • AUTO: the default. It chooses for each light: while its color temperature channel can reach the fire's deepest embers, the fire rides that channel, and a fire that goes redder than that moves to red, green and blue. It does not switch with the flicker; it moves when you lower the fader. On a light with only a color temperature channel, the fire stops at the lowest temperature it can reach.
  • CCT: rides the temperature channel, so the light makes the white it was calibrated for. The deepest embers stop at the lowest temperature it can reach.
  • RGB: rides the red, green and blue channels. It can paint the deep reds of the embers that a temperature channel cannot.

There are two tubes. Both carry a faint shimmer.

  • FLUO FLICKER: keeps flickering, never the same way twice. How Often sets how thick the flicker is, with STEADY, CRACKLE and UNEASY beside it. At 0 only the shimmer is left.
  • FLUO RESTART: nothing happens by itself. Pressing it, or a Scene recalling it, puts the tube out, the ends glow orange, it misfires and lights again. HIT does the same as often as you like.

The full list

GroupEffects
BasicBLINK, STROBE, PULSE, DOUBLE, JITTER, SPARKLE, RARE FLASH, RUNNER, FADE RUN, COMET, DRAW
LightsCANDLE, TORCH, FIREPLACE, CAMPFIRE, BONFIRE, FLUO FLICKER, FLUO RESTART, LIGHTNING, PAPARAZZI, TV, NEON, SIGNAL
PlacesBEACON R/B, BEACON BLUE, BEACON RED, BEACON AMBER, TOKYO, OSAKA, KYOTO, NARA, PACHINKO, WATER, FIREWORKS, LANTERNS, RAINBOW
MoveDRIFT, PASS, ORBIT, EIGHT, BOX, SPIRAL, SEARCH, NOD, SWEEP, LIGHTHOUSE, BREATHE, HANDHELD, WIND, JUMP, BALLYHOO
BeamZOOM PULSE, ZOOM BREATHE, IRIS PULSE, FROST BREATHE, GOBO SHAKE

In the Lights part of the effect list, the five fires come first as one block. Under them, one line describes the fire you have chosen (CANDLE, for example, is a quiet candle in still air).

RUNNER, FADE RUN and COMET need several fixtures, or pixels. Move and Beam appear when the selected fixtures support them.

Beside the name of an effect that changes color are up to four small swatches of the colors it runs, such as red and blue on BEACON R/B. An effect without them uses the color you set by hand.

Of the Move kinds, these move as follows.

  • NOD: moves the head up and down around where you placed it. Only Tilt moves.
  • SWEEP: swings Pan out to one side and back the same way.
  • LIGHTHOUSE: sweeps Pan one way like a lighthouse. It is dark while it swings back, so from the audience it seems to keep turning the same way. On a fixture with no Pan, it swings Tilt. One turn takes 10 seconds by default.
  • ORBIT, BOX, SPIRAL and BREATHE: turn around the position you placed. About 1 second after they start, their center moves to that position.

DRAW is a shape you draw yourself, for brightness. Its panel shows the shape with DRAW under it; DRAW opens a page to draw on, with Cancel and Done. A wide board sits under an overview of one whole cycle, every peak joined, with a mark moving where it is playing now.

PEAKS 1 to 4 sets how many peaks there are, and each peak is drawn in a shape of its own. Tap a section of the overview to spread that peak across the board; ALL lets you draw every peak in one stroke (only the peaks your finger crosses for at least a quarter of their section are rewritten). Draw from left to right: higher is brighter. Kanau joins the peaks so there is no step between them.

SMOOTH evens out the shake in your finger; SHARP keeps the corners and draws the sides straight. RANDOM, with two or more peaks, plays the peaks in a new order every round, never the same peak twice in a row, with an order of its own on each light. Speed is the speed of one peak, so four peaks make a cycle four times as long. With two or more peaks, BOUNCE, BUILD and SPELLER are not offered.

A stroke that covers less than a quarter of the width is refused, and the line before it stays. Until you draw, the shape is a soft rise and fall. Nothing is kept until Done. A setting stored in Saved keeps the line too.

SIGNAL — traffic lights

SIGNAL is a crossing. Tapping its name opens a panel of its own instead of applying anything.

A crossing has two roads, and each road carries a light for its cars and one for the people walking alongside it. The people get their green together with those cars. The four signals are CAR · ROAD 1, WALK · ROAD 1, CAR · ROAD 2 and WALK · ROAD 2.

Each signal is a card. Inside it sits a round icon for the whole signal, marked ALL, and beside it the lamps in a housing of their own — G Y R for the cars, R G for the people, in the order the chosen country hangs them. An empty circle carries +, and the number of fixtures in the signal is under the name.

To fill a signal:

  1. Select the fixtures on Home, then open SIGNAL.
  2. Tap an empty circle. A panel opens with the selected fixtures already ticked.
  3. Tap Done to put them in.

Tapping a circle with nothing selected opens the same panel to choose from. Which fixtures a circle takes depends on the circle.

  • The ALL circle: takes a fixture that is the whole signal and changes color for every phase.
  • A lamp circle: takes fixtures that light only for that lamp.

A fixture picked for more than one lamp has its pixels divided between them. Pixels you placed by hand stay where you put them. Such a fixture is listed, ticked, in each lamp's panel. Untick it to take it out of that lamp only.

One light source cannot be in more than one lamp at once.

The two lines at the top say where the crossing stands — ⏸ WAITING · CAR · ROAD 1 · GREEN, with what NEXT will reach underneath and a bar for the run to it. While it runs the first word is RUNNING; between two stops, CHANGING.

ButtonWhat it does
PLAYRuns from where it is. Without REPEAT it stops at the head of the cycle, where ROAD 1 gets its green
PAUSEHolds where it is, mid-phase if need be
BACKGoes to the previous change
NEXTGoes to the next change
REPEATKeeps the cycle running by itself

A change is the moment a signal comes to a lamp it can stay on. It counts for a signal that has fixtures in it and whose button is lit under NEXT STOPS AT. Yellow, and red with yellow, are passed through. With people lights, their green and their flashing green are changes too.

NEXT STOPS AT is the row just above BACK and NEXT, with four buttons: CAR 1, WALK 1, CAR 2 and WALK 2. All four are lit at first.

  • Turning one off: NEXT no longer stops for that signal. The signal still changes in order and at its real pace, and only the waits in between are cut short.
  • The last one: the last lit button does not go off.
  • A signal with no fixtures: its button is dim and does not light.

Below the buttons sit the country and Advanced. A button beside Advanced chooses the signal you are editing. Advanced holds the following.

  • How long each lamp holds: set with − 40s +.
  • The color of each lamp: changed in the color panel.
  • RESET: returns to that country's starting values.

One cycle stays 90 seconds. What you add to one phase comes out of the longest one.

SIGNAL 1 ▾ at the top switches between crossings and + NEW adds one. Each crossing keeps its own clock, country and signals.

Opening SIGNAL with fixtures that are in no crossing yet takes you to an empty crossing, and makes a new one when none is empty. Fixtures already in a crossing open that crossing.

Back in the EFFECT panel, when every selected fixture is in a crossing, the top of the panel shows that crossing's two lines. The row of buttons under it (BACK, NEXT, PLAY or PAUSE, and REPEAT) drives that crossing. PAUSE lights amber while the crossing runs, and REPEAT while it is on. Applying an effect takes the fixtures out of the crossing, and the top goes back to the effect.

RELEASE ALL lets go of the crossings too. Their fixtures go back to their own light, and each crossing keeps its signals and settings. START ALL starts them again from the head of the cycle. A crossing holding a locked fixture stays on, even after RELEASE ALL.

Marquee — the old bulb-sign shapes

Marquee is a row of buttons in the panel, just under Basic. They are the shapes an old bulb sign ran, under the names the signs used. Pressing one sets the shape and the arrangement together. From there you adjust it with the same knobs as every other effect.

The number of steps does not depend on which button you press. Pressing one gives you a step for each light source you have selected. For the dark gaps of a real sign, add steps with + at the head of the icon row.

The color arrives as COLOR, set to the warm glow of old tungsten. KEEP runs it in the color you made on the fader instead.

PatternWhat it does
CHASEOne bulb runs along the sign
DARK CHASEAll lit but one, and the dark one runs
CRAWLTwo side by side run together
BOUNCERuns to the end and comes back the way it came
BUILDLights one by one, then all clear together
FILLFills from the front, then empties from the front
FLIP FLOPOdd and even take turns
FLASHAll on, all off
TWINKLEEach bulb blinks on its own
SPELLERSpells out, then flashes three times

DARK CHASE is CHASE with INVERT on, and FILL is BUILD with INVERT on. The same switch turns any of the running shapes inside out.

Speed is in hertz, as everywhere else. Depth is how dark an unlit step goes: below 100 it keeps a little glow, like a filament cooling. Direction, BACK and NEXT work as they do on the rest.

Layering LIGHT, MOVE and BEAM

One fixture can carry a LIGHT effect for intensity and color, a MOVE effect for the head, and a BEAM effect at once. Choosing another effect in the same lane replaces it. Cells take LIGHT only. On a fixture whose second light source has its own dimmer, such as the Aura ring of a MAC Aura XIP, LIGHT moves the main light only.

Opening the panel shows the first running lane, in the order LIGHT, MOVE, BEAM.

Managing what is running

Tap EFFECT on Home with nothing selected. The list opens, titled Effects: Applies To and an EFFECT button at the top, then a row for each running effect. When nothing is running it reads Nothing is running.

Each row has these four buttons in fixed places.

  • EDIT: opens that effect's settings in the same panel. ‹ at the top left goes back to the list.
  • RELEASE or START: a released effect stays in the list, marked RELEASED.
  • PAUSE or RESUME: while the effect is released, PAUSE is dim and cannot be pressed.
  • CLEAR: removes the effect from the list. It also removes one that is marked RELEASED.

EDIT, CLEAR and the row's chips act on that row's own lane only (the head or the intensity). So a blink and a figure-eight on one fixture stay apart.

n ∨ opens the fixture chips for that row; n ∧ folds them again.

  • ×: the × on a chip drops that one fixture.
  • +: adds what you have selected, a group, a model, or All.

RELEASE ALL and START ALL apply to everything. Each crossing has a row of its own (SIGNAL 1, SIGNAL 2 and so on), with EDIT and CLEAR.

Effects keep counting through a blackout. Unlocked fixtures go dark and pick the movement up where it is when you clear the blackout. On a locked fixture the effect keeps running, at the intensity it had when you locked it. Fixture Lock is covered in chapter 10.

10 Locks, safety and stepping back

What stops you making a mistake in the middle of a take, and what lets you undo one.

There are three kinds of lock

The word turns up in three places, and each protects something different.

NameWhat it protectsWhere
Fixture LockThe fixture's current output. Nothing you do changes the value (an effect running when you lock keeps running)The fixture panel
Scene LockWhat is stored in a SceneSettings on the Scene's row
SCREEN LOCKThe screen. Touches do nothingTop of the screen, or Strap Lock

SCREEN LOCK

Hold SCREEN LOCK at the top of the screen for 0.5 seconds. A short tap will not lock it.

While locked, a purple wash and hatching cover the screen. The values stay readable, and sending and fades carry on. To unlock, drag the purple slider in the middle about 82% of the way to the right. Let go early and it stays locked.

SCREEN LOCK is out of reach while a panel such as Patch is open. Strap Lock still locks over one.

Strap Lock locks the screen when the iPhone or iPad hangs upside down from a strap. Lifting the device does not unlock the screen. Slide right to unlock, as with SCREEN LOCK.

  • Default: on for iPhone, off for iPad. Switch it in Settings → Settings → SCREEN LOCK.
  • Upside down on iPad: it means the top of the screen tipping toward the floor, however the iPad is held. It does not lock if the screen turns with the iPad.

With the switch on, three buttons under it set how far the top of the device must tip below level before the screen locks: NORMAL (30°), the default, EASY (20°) and EASIEST (12°). The smaller the angle, the less tilt it takes.

It does not lock while a finger is on the screen or just after, while ZEN, STAGE or Settings is open, while the keyboard, a confirmation or a file picker is showing, or when the device lies flat. Over Patch, Scenes, the effect panels, GM, BATTERY SAVE and MOVE it does lock: the panel stays open underneath and is still there when you unlock, and it cannot be pulled down while locked.

Auto Unlock, a switch under the buttons that is off by default, changes what lifting does: with it on, the screen unlocks as soon as the device is turned upright, with no slide. It releases only a lock that Strap Lock put on, not one you set with SCREEN LOCK, and nothing happens while the device lies flat, on its side or face down.

Fixture Lock

WARNING

Fixture Lock holds a fixture's output where it is. The grand master, blackout, BATTERY SAVE, MIDI, the session, TAP and changes to the patch do not change it — press blackout and a locked fixture stays lit. The count of what is still lit during a blackout is shown next to the green 🔒 at the top of the screen. A Scene recall does not change it either. Locks and limits belong to the console, and no Scene records or applies them (chapter 08).

Hold a fixture's round icon and turn on Lock under SETUP in its panel. Use it when a light must not change. An effect running when you lock keeps running, at the intensity it had then (chapter 06).

While a fixture is locked, the screen shows it like this.

  • The round icon shows a green padlock.
  • ⏻ shows a large padlock in its place.
  • The fader carries green.
  • The number button shows no padlock.

A locked fixture does not go dark in normal use. To clear the lock, turn off Lock in the fixture panel. The output then returns to what Kanau is working out now, with the grand master, B.O., BATTERY SAVE and the rest applied.

The lock holds the values at the fixture's addresses and is saved with the show. A lock whose fixture has been deleted stays on those addresses. Release it with UNLOCK in DMX Monitor.

BATTERY SAVE

Dims only the fixtures you mark, for the waiting around between takes.

  1. Mark them in the fixture settings under BATTERY SAVE, or in Patch → Select Many → Battery. You can also mark them as you patch.
  2. Tap BATTERY SAVE at the top of the screen. The marked fixtures dim.
  3. Tap it again to bring them back.

Hold it to set the brightness the fixtures keep and how long the fade takes. Brightness offers 75%, 50%, 35%, 25% and 0%, and 50% is the default. The fade is SNAP, 0.5, 1, 1.5 or 2 seconds, 1.5 by default, and starts and lands gently.

While it is on, the button, the band at the top of the screen and its edge turn green. The button now and then shows the brightness the fixtures keep, such as 50%.

  • GM: it multiplies with the grand master.
  • Locked fixtures: left alone.
  • A fader set as a switch: not dimmed. But if its fixture is marked, it goes OFF while BATTERY SAVE is on.
  • With nothing marked: the button is dim and does not turn on. Hold it to reach its settings.

While it is on, a dimmed fixture's fader fills only as high as the light really is. The part held back shows as a shadow with a green ↓. The ↓ fades in once the light has finished dropping, and disappears at once when the light starts to return.

To bring one fixture back for now, tap RELEASE in the green band just under the title of its panel. It turns into an amber RELEASED, and the fixture stays back until BATTERY SAVE is turned off.

At 0%, only the BATTERY SAVE fixtures go out. Unlike B.O., every other fixture stays lit, and no fader moves.

This dims your lights. It is not an iPhone battery setting.

HISTORY

Tap or hold HISTORY on Home to see the states you have been through. Choose a row to go back to it. HERE marks where you are.

At the head of the list, UNDO ↓ and REDO ↑ move HERE back or forward one step without closing the list. The arrow shows which way HERE moves. A line under them says what was undone or redone. With nowhere to go, they dim and shake.

  • It keeps the last 50. Going back and then working leaves the old states in place and adds the new one at the end.
  • It covers intensity, color, output on and off, limits, raw values, effects, GM, B.O., the group masters, the patch and the order of the faders.
  • Stepping back past a patch change keeps the list, and you can step forward again. A deleted fixture comes back with its place in Scenes and in values saved under a name.
  • Each patch edit, and each press of B.O. or a GM key, is a step of its own. RELEASE in BATTERY SAVE and anything done in BLIND are not in it.
  • Fixture Lock is outside it. A locked fixture does not move when you step back.
  • Scene recalls are recorded. Stepping back or forward across one also puts back which Scene is current, so AUTO UPDATE does not record into the wrong one. Overwriting a Scene's contents cannot be undone here; REVERT returns a Scene to how it was when you recalled it (chapter 08).
  • You cannot pull out one change on its own. You go back to the whole state at that moment.
  • It is kept with each show on this device. Quitting and reopening Kanau, or opening the show again, brings it back.

The fade when you recall a point in the history is set by Recall Fade Time, in the HISTORY list. HISTORY, UNDO and REDO cannot be pressed with nothing to go back to, during a Scene fade, while you hold a fader, or on a guest in a session.

11 Saving and sharing shows

A show holds one job: the patch, the groups, the order of the faders, the Scenes and the current look, with its Fixture Locks.

There is nothing to press. Changes are saved as you make them.

When it saves

WhatWhen
Patch, groups, order of the faders, ScenesAs you change them
The current look and fixture settingsWithin about two seconds of a change, and when the app goes to the background

The next launch restores the last show as it was saved, and the Scene you had recalled.

  • When the Scene is not restored: when that Scene has been deleted, or when you quit in BLIND.
  • Output: not restored. Kanau opens with output off (chapter 02).
  • UPDATE: under MANUAL UPDATE, changes you had not recorded yet still light UPDATE after reopening.

The very last change before a quit is not guaranteed to be saved. Use Export Show File when you need a file to keep or to hand on. The shows folder can be seen in the Files app.

Settings → Shows

ItemWhat it does
Current ShowRenames the show you are in
VersionsEarlier states of the current show. Restore goes back to one; the show as it is now is kept as a version first
Save AsStores the current state as another show and carries on in the copy
Export Show FileSaves first, then asks what to take (see below the table). Then choose where from the share sheet
Import Show FileAdds a .kanau to Other Shows as a new show and asks before opening it. Your current show is untouched
New ShowName it and tap Create. You get an empty show, and Patch opens
Other ShowsOpens a stored show. ⧉ duplicates. × moves it to Discarded, after a confirmation titled with its name

Notes on the table:

  • What Export Show File takes: All is the whole show. Patch and Groups takes the fixtures, their numbers, addresses and names, the fader order and the groups, without Scenes or the current look. Patch Only leaves out the groups as well.
  • Import Show File and device settings: this device's settings do not change unless you choose Use when the show opens (see Device settings that travel with a show, below).

The show you are in is named in amber beside Shows and carries a check under Current Show.

Starting a new show, or opening another, asks first. It shows Keep Show 1?, with what is in the show, and Keep, Discard or Cancel. It does not ask whether to save. Saving has already happened, so the question is whether to keep.

  • Discard: it is red but it does not delete. The show moves to Discarded, where Restore brings it back. To remove one for good, use its × there and confirm.
  • When it does not ask: a show with no fixtures and no Scenes does not ask this.
  • When you open another show: the question also says that Kanau's output switches to that show.

Versions are kept on this device. Versions appears under Current Show once there is one.

  • While the show changes, about one is made an hour.
  • One more is made before each restore.
  • After 10, the oldest goes.

Show names follow these rules.

  • A name that starts with ".", ends in ".history" or "-cues", or contains "/" or ":" cannot be used.
  • Names that differ only in capital letters count as the same name.

A .kanau that arrives by Files or AirDrop can be opened with Kanau and goes into Other Shows as a new show; while BLIND is on, it is refused with a vibration. A .kanaumidi is treated as a MIDI mapping file.

Whether it comes from Import Show File, Files or AirDrop, an imported show does not open straight away: you are asked first. What you are asked depends on the current show.

  • The current show has fixtures or Scenes: it is the same Keep Show 1? with Keep, Discard or Cancel as when you open another show.
  • The current show has no fixtures and no Scenes: the title is the imported show's name, such as Open Show 2?. It says that Kanau's output switches to that show, and you choose Open or Cancel.

Cancel keeps you in the current show with the light unchanged, and the imported show stays in Other Shows. If it arrives while a panel other than Settings is open, the question comes when you close that panel.

Opening and recovery

With nothing stored, the demo show opens. An older show that has no stored look opens with the intensity down.

If the file cannot be read you get Saved patch could not be read. Showing an empty rig; the file is left as it is., and it starts empty. The original file is kept and not overwritten.

A failed save shows Patch was not saved. in red. Chapter 14 covers what to do.

What is not in the show

WhatWhere it lives
Saved effect settingsOn the device, available to every show
Custom FixturesOn the device. The definitions of patched fixtures are kept in the show as well
Stored ★ colors and temperaturesOn the device. Colors per model and mode, temperatures shared
MIDI mappingOn the device. Exportable on its own as .kanaumidi
Output, Session, display settings, languageOn the device. Whether output is sending is not kept: it is off at every launch
HISTORYOn the device, one for each show
VersionsOn the device, beside each show. Not shown in the Files app
Piano ＋ / Piano −, Strap LockOn the device
Fixture UsageOn the device, for 180 days

Device settings that travel with a show: of the device settings, these are also saved as a copy with the show.

  • The MIDI and keyboard assignments
  • The output destination
  • The fade times
  • The color Favorites
  • The Patch Favorites

Their real home is still this device. The copy is there for when the show is opened on another device.

When you open a show that carries a copy, and the copy differs from this device's settings, you are asked once: Use this show's settings?. Use takes the show's settings, and Keep leaves this device's as they are. Which network connection is used, Session, and whether output has been started do not travel.

Settings → Settings

This holds the following.

  • The language (System or one of 15 languages)
  • The various fade times
  • The BATTERY SAVE brightness
  • Piano ＋ and Piano −
  • Strap Lock
  • ZEN TILT
  • The All row in Patch
  • Whether gels appear

Fixture Usage opens from here too. A new language applies after you quit and reopen Kanau. Text size follows the iOS setting.

Fixture Usage

Fixture Usage, above About in Settings → Settings, opens a record of which fixtures were touched and when. It records fixtures moved by hand or by a Scene, and fixtures with their faders up when sending started. It does not show how long a light was on, whether it actually came on, or whether it was on site. The record stays on this device for 180 days and is not part of the show file.

  • At the top, Last Operation and Last MIDI Input show the last operation and the last MIDI input, with the time. Starting and stopping sending show as SEND ON and SEND OFF. Turning a universe's output on and off shows as UNIVERSE ON and UNIVERSE OFF. A guest's operation shows as CHILD.
  • Below that, choose the day (All Days or one day) and the order (Last Touched, Number or Model), and use Search.
  • The menu to the left of Search narrows the list to one model or to a group in the open show, with a count for each. It is not shown when there is only one thing to choose.
  • Each fixture shows its number and model, its name, show and address, and when it was last touched. Tap a row to see the first and last time it was touched on each day.
  • Under the heading Patched, No Record are fixtures that are on the patch with no record. This does not mean they were not used or not on site.

At the bottom are these three.

  • Record Usage: stops the recording. It starts on.
  • Export CSV: writes the record for the chosen day (or all days, with All Days) to a CSV file.
  • Delete History: deletes all records on this device. It cannot be undone.

A guest in a session does not record its own operations. The host records them as CHILD.

12 MIDI controllers (Advanced)

Mapping the knobs and buttons of a MIDI controller onto fixtures and controls.

Connecting and mapping

  1. Turn on MIDI Controller in Settings → MIDI. It is off by default.
  2. Check that your gear appears under Inputs (None when there is none) and that Last CC or Last Note changes as you move a knob or press a button.
  3. Start with MIDI Channel on OMNI, then narrow it to 1–16 if you need to. OMNI receives all channels, 1–16; choose a number to receive only that channel.
  4. Map with Learn under Faders & Switches or Buttons. Both start folded as a whole; tap a heading to open it. Folding a section cancels a Learn waiting inside it.
  5. Turn a knob while Turn… is showing. For a button, press it while Press… is showing. Closing Settings first cancels Learn, and nothing is mapped.

Kanau is made for controllers that send absolute CC values (for example, the Behringer X-Touch Mini).

Bluetooth MIDI, inside the Inputs box just below Inputs, opens the system screen that finds Bluetooth MIDI devices and connects to them. Connected devices appear under Inputs, and are mapped with Learn like any other.

What a knob follows

A knob follows a position on screen, not a fixture. Change page or group and its target changes with it.

Faders & Switches lists the positions in order.

  • How many: 10 on an iPhone. On an iPad, one for each fader on screen, up to 40.
  • Fader N: takes a knob.
  • Switch N: indented under its Fader N. It takes a button.
  • Order: GRAND MASTER comes after the last Fader, then Buttons.

A knob on a fader set as a switch switches it as it passes the middle.

Mappings made per fixture in an earlier version are not carried over; map the screen positions again.

When a knob does nothing at first

If the knob and the value on screen disagree, nothing moves until the knob passes the value on screen. That is deliberate: it stops the level jumping.

The knob also has to pass the value again in these cases.

  • After you change page or group
  • After you unlock a fixture
  • After something else moves the value the knob has picked up (a Scene recall, a finger on screen, a Scene button or the GM chip)

While a fixture is locked, its knob does not pick it up. On a guest in a session, MIDI input is off.

With MIDI Controller on, turn on Send Values Back and Kanau sends each knob's current level back to the controller. Empty positions come back as 0. With MIDI Channel on OMNI, it sends on channel 1.

Buttons, and the mapping file

Under Buttons you can map:

  • FINE, PIANO, Page ‹ and Page ›.
  • BATTERY SAVE, which does what its button at the top does.
  • B.O., which turns the blackout on and off with each press. Fixtures with Lock on do not go out.
  • BACK and NEXT, which do what they do in Scenes.
  • UPDATE and SAVE, which do what they do in Scenes, when those can be pressed.
  • each Scene, and Switch N, which presses the ⏻ under Fader N and does what that fixture's Power Switch says.

Scenes folds away; its heading keeps the count, with · N learned once any Scene has a Note. Deleting a Scene removes its Note. One button carries one action. Fixture Lock applies to MIDI as well.

While BLIND is on, MIDI changes only the copy, except GRAND MASTER and B.O., which still act on the lights.

Export and Import under MIDI Map File write and read the mapping as a .kanaumidi file, separate from the show. An invalid file is refused with This file could not be read., and the current mapping stays.

Keys on a keyboard

A keyboard connected to the iPhone or iPad can do the same jobs as MIDI buttons. Keyboard is in Settings → MIDI, after Buttons. It is folded as a whole too; tap its heading to open it.

  1. Turn on Keyboard Input.
  2. Press a key and check that Last Key shows it.
  3. Tap Learn beside a job and press a key while Press… is showing.

The jobs are the same list as Buttons, with Switches and Scenes folded under it. The keys are kept in the MIDI mapping file.

  • Keys you have not learned do nothing.
  • Kanau ignores keys while you are typing in a text field.
  • Keys also work on a guest in a session.
  • Keys do nothing while LITE MODE is on.

13 Working from several devices — Session

iPhones and iPads on one show. Only the host sends DMX; the others watch, and work the same show through it once the host taps Allow.

A session lets devices on the same network drive one show. A guest sends what you do to the host. If the host stops, nothing takes over automatically. Every device in a session must run the same version of Kanau.

Who holds what

HostGuest
Sending DMXYesNo
Owns the showYesBorrows it
Changing the patchYesNo
Where a Scene is savedThe host's showSent to the host
Working the lightYesOnce the host taps Allow

When both touch the same fixture, the host wins. The guest sees IN USE BY and the other device's name (TAKEN when it has none).

Starting a session

  1. On the device that will send, choose Settings → Session → Host. A QR code appears. Until the device is on Wi-Fi or a wired network, the section says The code appears here when this device is on Wi-Fi or a wired network. Once it is, the code appears by itself.
  2. On the other device, choose Settings → Session → Join, then Scan Code.
  3. Point the camera at the host's QR code. The first time, Kanau asks to use the camera.
  4. Check for Joined and the connection state.

There is no number to type: the QR code is the only way in. A code from a host on an older version is not read. Keep every device on the same version.

These messages can appear while joining.

  • Camera access is off. Allow it in Settings to join.: camera access is turned off.
  • This is not a Kanau session code.: the QR code you read is not Kanau's.
  • Looking for the host…: the guest has not reached the host yet.

A guest starts out watching. Until the host taps Allow, nothing the guest touches reaches the light. During that time the status line reads WATCH ONLY, and the Session section says Waiting for the host to allow control.

Once the host taps Allow, the status line reads JOINED. Up to 8 guests can control at once.

Joining from the iPhone's Camera

The iPhone's own Camera app reads the code too: point it at the host's QR code and open the link it offers, and Kanau opens and joins, even if it was not running.

  • If this device is sending DMX, Kanau asks first with Joining stops this desk from sending., and Join or Cancel.
  • If it is already in another host's session, it asks with Joining switches to another host.

When it does not join

A Join box says why, and OK closes it:

ShownWhy
This code is not a Kanau session.The link is not a Kanau session code
This desk is hosting a session. Leave it first, then scan again.This device is a host
BLIND is on. Turn it off, then scan again.BLIND is on
LITE MODE is on. Leave it, then scan again.LITE MODE is on

The host's list

With Hosting on, the host's Session section shows the QR code, New Devices, New Code, and Devices: one row for each guest, with its name and Pending, Can control or Watching. The heading counts how many can control, such as 2 of 8 can control.

ControlWhat it does
AllowLets that guest work the light. A guest that has just joined is Pending, and only watches
Take BackReturns it to Watching. It releases whatever it was holding
RemoveDrops it. It cannot join again until you tap New Code, and it sees The host removed this device.
New DevicesWhen this is off, no new guest can join, and one that tries sees The host is not accepting new devices. Guests already in stay
New CodeAsks first, then drops every guest and makes a new QR code. A guest with the old code sees The host's code has changed. Scan the new code.

Once 8 guests can control, Allow is not offered.

What a guest can do

This is for a guest the host has allowed; a guest that is watching can do none of it.

The guest canThe host doesEach device keeps its own
Faders, color and gels, on fixtures and cellsAdding, removing and changing the patch, names, labels, SwitchWhich group and page is showing, which tab
Recalling Scenes, BACK and NEXT in the Play row, SAVE to store, UPDATE into the recalled Scene, and AUTO UPDATE / MANUAL UPDATE, which is shared with the hostReordering Scenes, deleting, renaming, fade, lock; HISTORY; BLINDFINE, 10 / 5, PIXELS, PIANO mode
⏻, GM, B.O., BATTERY SAVE with its amount and RELEASE for one fixtureOutput, Shows, DMX MonitorDisplay settings, language, gels, Strap Lock
Limits, Fixture Lock, clearing a selection, reordering the fadersFade times, Piano ＋ / Piano −, Power SwitchMIDI mapping, stored ★ colors

The PIXELS and FIXTURES sections of the COLOR panel (chapter 05) appear on the host only.

  • Storing a Scene: a Scene stored from the guest is written by the host. While a fade is running, the host refuses SAVE with Not accepted.
  • The guest's show: the guest's own show file is untouched. Leave Session puts it back.
  • Opening or importing a show: not possible while you are a guest. The tap is refused with a vibration.

Effects and the guest

Every effect action reaches the host.

ActionFrom the guest
Applying an effectWorks
PAUSE and RESUMEWorks
RELEASE, on the fixtures you selectedWorks
RELEASE ALLWorks
EDIT, RELEASE, START, PAUSE, RESUME and CLEAR on a row of the running effects (EFFECT with nothing selected)Works
Clearing a cell's effectsWorks
SIGNAL: BACK, NEXT, PLAY, PAUSE, REPEAT, NEXT STOPS AT, Advanced, and filling the signalsWorks
START ALLWorks

Working at the same time, and losing the link

What the guest changes appears on the guest's screen at once. If the host touches the same fixture, the host wins and the guest sees IN USE BY and the host's name. A fixture the other device is working shows a cyan edge with a name.

ConnectionState
GreenConnected to the host
AmberNothing from the host for about 3 seconds
RedNothing for about 15 seconds. The host is no longer available. appears

If the link drops, the guest keeps showing the last state. It does not leave on its own, so use Leave Session. After reconnecting, faders are still relative.

No internet is needed. The devices must be able to reach each other on the same network. Client isolation, a firewall and similar settings can block the session even where DMX gets through.
